💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that it’s hard to believe the entire Critical Role table for Campaign 4 hasn’t been together since the Convergence arc in June.
  • Since Critical Role Campaign 4 episode 31, "Trick of the Light," Critters haven’t seen hide nor hair of everyone’s favorite orc Druid, Thaisha Lloy.
  • In a recent development, luckily, the wait is finally over.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that it’s hard to believe the entire Critical Role table for Campaign 4 hasn’t been together since the Convergence arc in June. Since then, the Soldiers, Seekers, and Schemers tables have remained separate. Or, more accurately, the Seekers and Schemers tables have remained separate.

Since Critical Role Campaign 4 episode 31, "Trick of the Light," Critters haven’t seen hide nor hair of everyone’s favorite orc Druid, Thaisha Lloy. Nor have they received any confirmation about when, exactly, Travis Willingham will return with a new character, after his Paladin, Teor Pridesire, met an unfortunate end in episode 30, "Here in the Dark.".

In a recent development, luckily, the wait is finally over. Critical Role unveiled on Nov. 23 that its eagerly anticipated Soldiers table, featuring Aabria Iyengar as Thaisha, will return on Dec. 3 and Dec. 10 for a two-part Soldiers table arc. And she won’t be alone.

Industry observers note that when the three tables split off in June last year, it seemed that the Soldiers table would consist only of Thaisha. In an interview with Polygon, Iyengar confirmed she wasn't sure at the time whether Thaisha’s story would be told through cold openings or off-camera. Later, however, the Critical Role team decided to give the Soldiers table a mini-arc following Thaisha as she explored her future on the druidic path. But she would not be doing all of that on her own.

“We’ve got some amazing guests, Celia Rose Gooding and Abubakar Salim," Iyengar told Polygon. "Two people who I have admired for so long; it was so fun to finally sit down and play with them. And, of course, the return of Travis Willingham and his new PC.”.

Willingham has been absent from Critical Role’s Campaign 4 since his katari Paladin, Teor Pridesire, died in episode 30. Teor was killed inside House Tachonis’s Obrimus Manor during a truly heartbreaking moment for the fans and the cast.

Gooding and Salim have both guest-starred on Critical Role before: Gooding appeared in Exandria Unlimited: Divergence as the half-elf Rei’nia Saph, while Salim has played various roles, most recently the fungril Berserker Mercy in Age of Umbra: Sallowlands.

Though Iyengar couldn’t reveal what characters Willingham and the other guests would play in this two-episode arc, she told Polygon they were all “deeply connected and bound by a similar purpose.”.

In a recent development, “Dol-Runja is the seat of the orcs and the druids in Kahan. So it's important and interesting to see multiple facets of that.”.

Since June, the Seekers and Schemers tables have been dealing with assassination attempts at the theater, watery heists, and literal hell. When we last checked in, the Seekers table — with the help of several NPCs like fey pixie Clauny the Rose, talking dog Dame Morgaine, and scoundrel Pimley Morn — successfully rescued the daughters of their ally, Ulbid Morn.

Industry observers note that on Dec. 3, Critters will reunite with Thaisha, who set off for the city of Dol-Rungja. There, she hopes to speak with the Druidic people and persuade them to abandon their neutrality and help fight back against the Sundered Houses.

Sources indicate that whether that will work out for Thaisha remains to be seen. The last time she encountered other druids, a few of them weren’t too pleased with her role in bringing the Necromancer Wizard, Occtis Tachonis (Alexander Ward), back to life as a Hollowed One. Given that she’ll have to answer for it to very notable people, including her grandma, we expect the orc druid to be put through the proverbial wringer over the course of her two-episode arc.

In a recent development, aabria Iyengar, Travis Willingham, and guest stars Celia Rose Gooding and Abubakar Salim begin their Soldiers adventure on Dec. 3.

Tech Report: A Doctor Doom And Doctor Strange Team-Up Is One Of The Best Marvel Comics Ever

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (917 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Slashfilm

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that doctor Victor von Doom is a master of magic, so little surprise he's often crossed paths with the Sorcerer Supreme, Doctor Stephen Strange.
  • Industry observers note that written by Roger Stern, one of the best writers in the 1980s Marvel Comics bullpen, and drawn by Mike Mignola, future creator of the "Hellboy" universe, "Triumph and Torment" is indeed a triumph.
  • Doom's usual nemeses, Reed Richards and the Fantastic Four, are nowhere to be seen.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that doctor Victor von Doom is a master of magic, so little surprise he's often crossed paths with the Sorcerer Supreme, Doctor Stephen Strange. Their first meeting, and the foundation for their mutual respect, was in 1989's "Doctor Strange and Doctor Doom: Triumph and Torment," one of the essential Doctor Doom comics every Marvel fan should read.

Industry observers note that written by Roger Stern, one of the best writers in the 1980s Marvel Comics bullpen, and drawn by Mike Mignola, future creator of the "Hellboy" universe, "Triumph and Torment" is indeed a triumph. It was published in the "Marvel Graphic Novel" line, itself designed to tell standalone and more mature stories featuring Marvel's character stable.

Doom's usual nemeses, Reed Richards and the Fantastic Four, are nowhere to be seen. While, conceptually, Doom needs Richards, tales like "Triumph and Torment" prove how he can hold individual stories without the FF. "Triumph and Torment" is also one of the most convincing arguments for Doom being more than a villain.

Industry observers note that in Doom's debut, Stan Lee and Jack Kirby's "Fantastic Four" #5, it's established he had, during his and Reed's time at college, been obsessed with dark magic and built a machine to enter the nether world, which blew up and scarred him. His fuller origin in "Fantastic Four Annual" #2 revealed his ambition was to contact his mother, Cynthia von Doom, a witch who died during his childhood. Cynthia's trunk of magical secrets begat Victor's own knowledge of sorcery.

A 1971 story in "Astonishing Tales" #8 (by Gerry Conway and Gene Colan) then revealed that every Midsummer's Eve (when the liminal walls between worlds are the thinnest), Doom battles the forces of Hell to free his mother's soul, only to reach a stalemate. So, in "Triumph and Torment," Doom does the unthinkable and asks for help.

In "Triumph and Torment," both Strange and Doom partake in a contest of the world's greatest sorcerers held by Strange's god-like patrons, the Vishanti. Strange wins with Doom placing second — a familiar place for him, but it works in his favor. Per contest rules, Strange must grant a "boon" of Doom's choosing, and Doom wants Strange's assistance in freeing his mother's soul.

"Is one woman's soul beneath the notice of the Sorcerer Supreme?" Doom asks a surprised Strange, who in turns questions why Doom never requested his help before. "I will bear any ordeal, Strange, but Doctor Doom does not beg," he replies. That pride is ultimately crucial to Doom's proposal to free Cynthia.

In Hell, facing the overwhelming power of the demon lord Mephisto, Doom seemingly trades Strange's soul for his mother's. But Cynthia, a noble woman, refuses and spurns Victor — a sacrifice that secures her place in Heaven. Doom finally frees his mother and outwits her devilish captor. This plan both flatters and damns Doom's character. He values his mother's safety more than her love for him, but his own pride most of all.

"Triumph and Torment" helps itself stand alone by exploring Doom and Strange's origins, so you can understand both men completely from this one story. Their journeys are also quite similar, as physical injuries prompt both men to venture high into the Himalayas seeking mystical knowledge. The book retells Cynthia's death, and Victor's childhood, via Doom's attendant Boris. Along with the reader, Strange realizes that beneath Doom's cold armor lies a child of tragedy. Upon taking his mask for the first time, Doom swears that pain and compassion are for lesser men — but his blueprint to free his mother, and what it costs him, prove otherwise.

In a recent development, mike Mignola's art in "Triumph and Torment" makes Doctor Doom, his castle, and Latveria feel more truly gothic than in any other comic. Knowing Mignola went on to create a demonic superhero, too, it's hard not to compare "Triumph and Torment" to "Hellboy." Mignola drawing Strange and Doom facing down demons feels like a "Hellboy" test run in the same way his Batman comic "Sanctum" was.

Recent findings suggest that in the documentary "Mike Mignola: Drawing Monsters," Mignola admitted he felt out of place drawing typical Marvel superhero books during the 1980s. "I'm not cut out to draw superheroes [...or] cars and buildings, most of the stuff that comics are made of," Mignola explained. He'd much rather be drawing monsters, which is why "Triumph and Torment" was a perfect assignment for him. Mignola's penciling especially comes to vibrant life once Doom and Strange enter Hell.

It has been revealed that far from looking identical, the demons all have different skin tones, weapons, and proportions. Some have wings, one is a humanoid torso on a giant serpent's tail, etc. Inker/colorist Mark Badger, rather than using a single background color for Hell, employs red-orange-yellow-green gradients. Mixed with Mignola's heavy shadows, it looks truly creepy, ethereal, and dangerous, like the typical fire and brimstone version of Hell but made even stranger. Compare this to the scary and lonely underworld in Mignola's 2010s series "Hellboy in Hell," and you can see an artist who grew.

It has been revealed that of course, the greatest achievement in "Triumph and Torment" is Doctor Doom's. In "Astonishing Tales" #8, Doom's goal to free his mother from eternal damnation is presented as a Sisyphean task he'll never achieve. Thinking he could break the laws of Hell is a sign of Doom's immense self-regard and ambition — and incredibly, he eventually did it.

I Knew Blade Runner 2099 Reviews Would Praise The Visuals, But I’m Surprised By Critics’ Big Critique

💡 Key Takeaways

  • If there’s anything to know about the Blade Runner universe, it’s that it has major dystopian vibes, and that particular aura is definitely present in 2099.
  • According to recent reports, blade Runner 2099 is a disappointing continuation of the iconic series which leans too heavily into the dark and downbeat side of its future dystopia rather than finding ways to elevate its lead characters in that world.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Blade Runner 2099 has arguably been one of the most anticipated titles on the 2026 TV schedule, and there’s a good reason for that. Not only does it expand upon the classic science-fiction franchise, but it also has two capable leads in Michelle Yeoh and Hunter Schafer (who do plenty of stunt work). The show debuts later this week, and reviews are finally starting to roll in. Having seen the show in its entirety for myself, I figured there would be high praise for the visuals, but I am surprised by one particular critique amongst critics.

If there’s anything to know about the Blade Runner universe, it’s that it has major dystopian vibes, and that particular aura is definitely present in 2099. The series continues to highlight a version of Los Angeles in the distant future that’s far from pristine. Surprisingly enough, though, it seems that the show is proving to be a little too dark for some pundits’ liking. Scott Collura of IGN praises the visual style of the series, though he takes issue with just how bleak the proceedings get:.

According to recent reports, blade Runner 2099 is a disappointing continuation of the iconic series which leans too heavily into the dark and downbeat side of its future dystopia rather than finding ways to elevate its lead characters in that world. Michelle Yeoh and Hunter Schafer are both miscast as a buddy-cop team that subsist on fear and mistrust and angst, while the more interesting characters don’t get nearly enough to do. While the production design, visual effects and overall look of the show are a wonder to behold, 2099 also leans so heavily into its creators’ own fandom at times that it can be distracting.

2099 – which, of course, takes place 50 years after 2017’s Blade Runner 2049 – sees Replicants having become the ruling class, while humans are treated like vermin. At the center of the story is Cora (Hunter Schafer), a human trying to escape her circumstances by posing as a Replicant Blade Runner. In the process of doing that, she is partnered with Olwen (Yeoh), a dying Replicant Runner. The story does indeed get dark, but I didn’t have much of an issue with it. As for The Guardian’s Rhik Samadder, though, he states:.

If you’re a cyberpunk who mainlines ennui and likes watching actors you can’t see, speaking words you can’t hear, this show may well knock your fishnet socks off. But why spend this much time immersed in a doomed world, when you could open up a window and watch the real one? It’s live!

Samadder also notably calls the visuals both “impressive” and “oppressive” in a way. However, also mentioning that the series also “plunges us into a far darker world” than the Blade Runner movies (which don’t directly tie into 2099). Likewise, Aaron Pruner of CNET isn’t really a fan of the overly dark setting and aesthetic. In his somewhat mixed review, Pruner praises the show’s execution while also posing this question regarding the bleak vibe:.

In a recent development, could a little bit of levity help break up the monotony? Possibly. But, again, that would go against the grain of the Blade Runner franchise. And not for nothing, the original wasn’t at all funny, yet nuanced characters like Roy Batty (Rutger Hauer) and Pris (Daryl Hannah) brought life and color to the dreary, rain-slick streets of Ridley Scott’s original.

It has been revealed that the darkness doesn’t seem to be deterring everyone, though, as Alison Herman of Variety has glowing thoughts on the show. Aside from praising Hunter Schafer, Herman also admires series creator Silka Luisa’s adherence to this storied continuity birthed by Philip K. Dick:.

Industry observers note that ‘Blade Runner 2099’ dutifully incorporates the franchise’s visual and thematic touchstones. Despite the passage of time, computer screens still have the blocky, vintage look of early PCs; a psychotically violent replicant named Clotilde (Amy Lennox), an early convert to a cult of personality that promises her and Olwen’s kind eternal life, is a clear echo of Daryl Hannah’s cartwheeling Pris from the original film. ‘Blade Runner’ has always hewn to the beats of a detective noir, and over time, has acquired mainstays of its own that ‘2099’ dutifully nods to.

That’s definitely a massive compliment, considering how beloved Ridley Scott’s original 1982 film is and how much critical praise Denis Villeneuve’s 2049 received. Still, not everyone is impressed. TVLine’s Dave Nemetz finds the sci-fi show to be overly bleak as well. Not only that, but he also isn’t too taken with the visuals like a number of others are:.

We get it: The L.A. of the future is a rough scene. But there's no spark of joy or hope here to offset the bleakness... just more bleakness. ‘2099’ should at least provide some sci-fi eye candy, but the visuals are a disappointing rehash of the sleek, neon-soaked aesthetic of the original ‘Blade Runner.’.

According to recent reports, although I can’t say I saw these critiques about the show’s vibe coming, I can’t blame others for not caring for its dark nature. To me, this kind of style is just baked into the DNA of the franchise, though I can admit that Blade Runner 2099 does delve into murkier territory at times. I’m curious as to how fans will feel when all eight episodes of the show become available for Prime Video subscription holders on November 25.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, if you thought the wait to finally hear Chris Evans' Steve Rogers announce (well, more like theatrically whisper), "Avengers, assemble!" in 2019's "Avengers: Endgame" was long enough, then that's nothing compared to the plight of "X-Men" enthusiasts ever since the first 20th Century Fox film came out in 2000. Arguably no fanbase has suffered more in that time, enduring a steady stream of relatively comic book-y blockbusters that mostly just seemed embarrassed of their own source material, with only a few exceptions thrown into the mix. Whatever you might say about "Avengers: Doomsday" leading up to its release, however, "comic book-y" has to be at the top of the list — and the final "Doomsday" trailer has just given us the famous line every nerd has been dying to witness.

Yes, this is a perfect excuse to link to the memorable "Say the line, Bart!" gag from "The Simpsons." "X-Men" fans have read it in the comics, they've actually seen it before in the animated "X-Men: '97" series, and it basically seemed like a fait accompli that Marvel would find a way to deliver this moment in live action for "Doomsday." You know what we're talking about: Cyclops (James Marsden), leader of the mutant team of superheroes, finally bellowing out, "To me, my X-Men!".

The only wrinkle is probably the idea of dropping this reveal in a trailer, as opposed to saving it for the movie itself. Would it have been ideal to experience this for the very first time in theaters on opening weekend, rather than on your phone while walking into work on a Monday morning? Of course! Does that make the actual scene any less thrilling? Probably not! So, without further ado, let's overanalyze this to within an inch of its life below.

Could anyone have imagined seeing this comic book panel come to life before their very eyes in "Avengers: Doomsday"? Okay, sure, the circumstances aren't exactly what most fans would've anticipated in a vacuum. Rather than seeing this moment occur after several successful "X-Men" movies spent years carefully laying the foundation for Scott Summers to become the leader of the team we know and love from the comics, this is getting shoehorned into a crossover movie pitting a few familiar "X-Men" film stars against a villain they have no real connection to in Robert Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom. And despite the "X-Men"-centric nature of this call to action, it's at least a little funny to hear him specifically assemble his fellow mutants and then watch several members of the Avengers and Fantastic Four arrive in perfect formation.

But between the awfully long wait for this moment and James Marsden's delivery of this dialogue (which is pretty similar to the one in Season 1 of the widely well-received "X-Men '97"), it's tough to imagine many fans out there will feel inclined to nitpick anything. Directors Joe and Anthony Russo are clearly hoping this begins to set things right for a group of mutants who've deserved a much better live-action fate than they've typically received. So, while the internet spends the next few weeks arguing over whether this sequence had the requisite amount of hype and payoff to decades of build up, the rest of the moviegoing population has probably already been convinced to fork over approximately $2 billion for this latest "Avengers" extravaganza. So it goes!

The Avengers, X-Men, Fantastic Four, and more will arrive in "Avengers: Doomsday" on December 18, 2026.

When Kate Middleton stepped out on the green carpet at the Earthshot Awards ceremony in Mumbai this week, it was “an absolute princess moment,” states British designer Amanda Wakeley.

In a recent development, “Catherine has really come into her own. She has found her stride and a new confidence, and you see that in this dazzling but also practical ‘tourdrobe,’’’ Wakeley, who has previously dressed the Princess of Wales and used to dress Princess Diana, tells Vanity Fair.

Recent findings suggest that it has been 10 years since Princess Kate last visited India. Her fashion choices are more sophisticated now than on her visit in 2016, and the speech she delivered at the Earthshot Prize ceremony on November 17 shows a fresh confidence. Kate’s flared floral dresses and the wedge shoes she used to love (but the late Queen Elizabeth apparently disliked) have been replaced by Manolo Blahnik pumps, couture power suits, and clothes by some of her favorite designers, such as Emilia Wickstead.

Prince William and Princess Kate attend The Earthshot Prize Awards Ceremony at the Jio World Convention Centre on November 17, 2026 in Mumbai, India.

It has been revealed that kate’s decision to wear a striking vermilion dress made from handwoven silk by New Delhi–based designer Mahima Mahajan to the Earthshot Prize ceremony spoke volumes. The eye-catching dress, which she paired with a burgundy Prada velvet clutch, was chosen after Kate had selected a special suite of emeralds from the royal gem collection. The green stones on the dress perfectly matched her jewels, which served as an homage to both Queen Elizabeth II and India, as the green of the Indian flag represents growth and prosperity.

It has been revealed that the dazzling stones known as the “emerald tassel suite” were worn frequently by the late Queen Elizabeth II, and while Kate has previously worn the earrings, this marked the first time she wore the set. The effect was dramatic.

“Never has Catherine looked more like a queen in waiting,” Wakeley claims of the look.

Sources indicate that wearing the suite ensured that Kate, who has free rein of the royal jewels, looked more regal than ever. “What was fascinating was seeing Catherine wear these incredible family heirlooms along with more relaxed collections from some of her favorite modern jewelry designers like Kiki McDonough and Astley Clarke,” remarks Wakeley.

Kate’s carefully curated wardrobe for the trip wasn’t just about power dressing—it was also about showing she can be sustainable as well as on trend.

In a recent development, “It was good to see Catherine making a proper nod to sustainability by rewearing her Roksanda dress,” Wakeley notes. “It’s clear a lot of thought has gone into her outfit choices. Her wardrobe has to be practical, and her clothes have to work harder than most people consider for their clothing; she needs weight in the hem of the floaty dresses. She has learned lessons the hard way. She is often seen bending down, talking to children, so she’s conscious of how low a neckline is, how short a skirt is.”.

Princess Kate visits the Nowrosjee Wadia Maternity Hospital, on November 18, 2026 in Mumbai, India.

For her visit to Mumbai’s Nowrosjee Wadia Maternity Hospital on November 18, Catherine chose a striking red tailored Emilia Wickstead skirt suit with Manolo Blahnik pumps. On November 16, she opted for a pistachio blazer by designer Veronica Beard, paired with white Alexander McQueen trousers and pearl-buckled Camilla Elphick flats, a relaxed and accessible look for when she picked up a cricket bat.

Princess Kate plays cricket on November 16, 2026 in Mumbai, India.

As Princess of Wales, Catherine is often compared to Princess Diana. “The main difference is Diana was a fashion icon. Catherine has become a style icon,” Wakeley notes. “There’s a significant difference. Diana played into the fashion of the day and was finding her style. During the time she resigned from public life, she worked out her style DNA. Catherine has had to do that on the job. Very wisely, she has worked out her style and doesn’t get too impacted by fashion and trends. She goes for what she likes. What works for her rather than trends. She really knows now what works for her.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, remember when Olivia Wilde was served child custody papers by Jason Sudeikis while she was on stage in front of thousands presenting Don’t Worry Darling at CinemaCon? That was over four years ago in the heat of the pair figuring out the post-split situation. However, these days, the two seem to be on better terms. To that point, Sudeikis is even crediting his ex for the creation of his massively successful TV show, Ted Lasso (which just got big news by the way).

Sudeikis recently noted two very notable things about his high-profile breakup. One of those came up when he was on Talk Easy with Sam Fragoso, during which he said his and Wilde's split was “more complicated” and “more human” than how it was portrayed in the media. And on another occasion, Sudeikis went out of his way to talk about how Wilde played a role in getting Ted Lasso made. In his words to the Smartless podcast:.

Sources indicate that I remember Olivia and I were out to dinner and she's like, 'What are you guys gonna do with that? Like, you guys love doing that thing so much. You should do something with that.' I was like, ‘Yeah.’ And then, her and I just started chatting about it at dinner a little bit like, ‘That would be fun.’.

Recent findings suggest that as Sudeikis shared during an interview at a special live edition of the show at the Hollywood Bowl in Los Angeles, Wilde was the person who actually followed up with her then-partner on the Ted Lasso idea years before him and the other creators knew what to do with the character. As Sudeikis continued:.

It has been revealed that then Joe and Brendan come out to New York and we hang out for a week in Brooklyn... And then for three days straight, we just start filling up pages of ideas and realize, ‘Oh, this might be a TV show.’ And then we didn't do anything with it for three years.

Recent findings suggest that wild, right? Mr. Ted Lasso himself, alongside two of his co-creators Brendan Hunt, Joe Kelly, sat on the idea for a while until one day they were overflowing with ideas. And then, they sat on it again until this happened. In Sudeikis’ words:.

It wasn’t until Bill Lawrence came to me with an idea for another TV show that I was like ‘Ah, this isn’t the right fit.’ He goes, ‘Well, if you have any ideas…’ I go, ‘Well, here’s a stack of papers of stuff we wrote down.’ And he read it, and was like, ‘Oh yeah, there’s definitely a show here.’.

According to recent reports, now that Ted Lasso is one of the best highlights to watch with an Apple TV subscription, it’s pretty crazy to think how long the whole process took. It took so long that when the idea was first formed Sudeikis and Wilde went from being an engaged couple to splitting up. Thankfully it did, because it’s one of my favorite shows on streaming in recent years.

In a recent development, and did you know there’s even a tribute to Olivia Wilde in Ted Lasso? The AFC Richmond locker room (at one point at least) features Wilde’s actual surname, “Cockburn,” alongside the names of other writers’ friends, family members and former mentors within the production.

Over the past summer, Olivia Wilde spoke a bit to her divorce as well, sharing the conversation that led to their split. Wilde is also having a big year herself, thanks to her latest directorial effort, The Invite, and Sudeikis says he’s “thrilled” for her success. As for him, he just got some good news, as Ted Lasso was just officially renewed for Season 5 by Apple. So the show remains the gift that keeps on giving. In short, thank you, Jason and Olivia!

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Speaking to the Independent back in 2023, Cillian Murphy admitted there was one Christopher Nolan movie that he would've liked to have worked on but didn't.
  • Murphy has, to date, appeared in six of Nolan's movies.
  • As for "Interstellar," Murphy told the Independent that while he wishes he could've been involved with it, he loves it all the same, explaining:.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Speaking to the Independent back in 2023, Cillian Murphy admitted there was one Christopher Nolan movie that he would've liked to have worked on but didn't. The film in question? Nolan's 2014 space odyssey "Interstellar.".

Murphy has, to date, appeared in six of Nolan's movies. He played Dr. Jonathan Crane, aka the Scarecrow, in Nolan's three Batman movies (albeit, two of those performances were cameos), and he portrayed Robert Fischer, a man subjected to dream invasion, in "Inception." He also played a soldier in "Dunkirk" and won an Academy Award for Best Actor for portraying the titular character in Nolan's "Oppenheimer." And while he's great in all these roles, some of Murphy's performances in Nolan's films are even better than others.

As for "Interstellar," Murphy told the Independent that while he wishes he could've been involved with it, he loves it all the same, explaining:.

"I adore 'Interstellar' just because I find it so emotional. [...] I remember seeing it in the cinema when I had little kids. It just had a substantial impact on me. It broke my heart. I love watching his films when I'm not in them because you don't have to freak out about the size of your ears, or whatever.".

That said, Murphy clarified that the "right people" were ultimately cast in "Interstellar." Indeed, the film is full of major-name stars, including Matthew McConaughey, Anne Hathaway, Jessica Chastain, John Lithgow, Michael Caine, Ellen Burstyn, Casey Affleck, Topher Grace, David Oyelowo, and Matt Damon. Given the prestige of that cast, Murphy likely would've been happy to tag in for any of those actors.

Cillian Murphy was interviewed by the Independent right around the time "Oppenheimer" opened in theaters, and it was brought to his attention that many filmgoers had, amusingly, paired the movie with Greta Gerwig's "Barbie" to create a deliberately incongruous double-feature widely referred to as "Barbenheimer." It was quite the cultural event as well, with "Barbenheimer" going on to become a massive box office success.

Playfully, the Independent asked Murphy which Christopher Nolan film he would pair "Oppenheimer" with, and he presented the following options:.

Industry observers note that "You could go 'Interstellar,' which is very ... explores similar scientific, physic themes. Or you could watch 'Dunkirk,' which is also set in World War II. 'Dunkirk' is shorter, so that might be a good match 'cause it's like an hour-and-a-half, and then you can go into ['Oppenheimer'].".

"Dunkirk" is, just for the record, 106 minutes, but I get Murphy's meaning. "Oppenheimer" is already three hours, and "Interstellar" is 169 minutes, so pairing two very long movies together might be a bit of a chore.

Nolan has since directed the 2026 mega-hit "The Odyssey," while, in the same year, Murphy made his long-awaited return to the "28" franchise by appearing briefly in "28 Years Later: The Bone Temple." One can assume, however, that Murphy and Nolan will cross paths again professionally in due time.

According to recent reports, if you were a tween or teen in the late '90s and early 2000s, then you probably had or knew someone who had a crush on Chad Michael Murray. While he first won over the hearts of millions as the teen heartthrob in the hit teen drama One Tree Hill and the beloved teen rom-com A Cinderella Story, Murray has continued to make audiences swoon over him in a plethora of romance movies, including a steady stream of Christmas-themed ones. I was bummed when I didn’t see his name in any of the upcoming Netflix releases or in Hallmark's Countdown to Christmas lineup, but it turns out Murray is in a upcoming Christmas movie, and it’s streaming right now.

It won’t be a Murray-less Christmas after all! The former teen heartthrob stars in Postcards for Christmas, which is available to anyone with an active Hulu subscription. The holiday flick centers on Hannah (Jessica Lowndes), who has traveled to Mistletoe Valley to temporarily help her college best friend run the local post office. When Hannah discovers a batch of love letter postcards that were never delivered, she becomes determined to reunite the star-crossed lovers. She teams up with Ford (Murray), the local radio DJ, and the pair read a postcard every day leading up to Christmas as they try to solve the mystery of who these letters could belong to.

It has been revealed that I happened to stumble on the film while scrolling through Hulu looking for something new to watch and knew I had to check it out. I’m so glad I did because Postcards for Christmas did not disappoint. Both Murray and Lowndes were great on screen together, and I really enjoyed the mystery angle of the romcom. It’s totally worth checking out, especially if you’re a fan of Murray.

I Just Found Out Chad Michael Murray Nearly Played A Different Character On One Tree Hill.

I should have known to check on Hulu’s holiday slate earlier, considering they’re really stepping up in the Christmas movie department lately, giving fans a upcoming place to check out holiday films outside of Netflix and Hallmark. It makes sense for Murray to appear on the streamer, considering it’s the current home to all nine seasons of One Tree Hill and several of his other romcoms, including last year’s holiday film Joy to the World.

It’s too early to say for sure, but it sounds like Murray might become Hulu’s go-to romantic lead for its Christmas flicks the same way Hallmark has been dominated by Lacey Chabert. I’m definitely not complaining!

After watching Postcards for Christmas and Joy to World, Murray fans should head over to Netflix to catch him in the 2024 film The Merry Gentlemen, which the internet had a field day with. The current Sullivan’s Crossing star also appears in holiday films on Lifetime, Great American Family, and Hallmark.

#165836. The 6 Most Outrageous GTA 6 Myths, Debunked

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1082 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Polygon ↗ Open Full Page

The 6 Most Outrageous GTA 6 Myths, Debunked

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1082 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Polygon

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, after a wild opening weekend, Grand Theft Auto 6 is off to the races.
  • Because of that, there are a lot of myths about GTA 6 currently floating around the internet.
  • The claim: GTA 6’s story forces you to do chores for Lucia instead of crimes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, after a wild opening weekend, Grand Theft Auto 6 is off to the races. Millions are playing Rockstar’s enormous open-world game and discovering its complexities in real time. There’s a lot to unpack in a game that’s filled with intersecting gameplay systems across a long story, and some players are already taking advantage of that. At the same time, the opening days of GTA 6’s launch have been filled with misinformation, much of it fueled by culture warriors and content creators looking to turn outrage into clicks on social media platforms that incentivize such behavior.

Because of that, there are a lot of myths about GTA 6 currently floating around the internet. Some come from harmless misunderstandings, while others are more deliberate misrepresentations intended to scare off potential players. To help you navigate the noise, we’ve rounded up some of the most rampant myths currently circulating around GTA 6 and fact-checked them accordingly.

The claim: GTA 6’s story forces you to do chores for Lucia instead of crimes.

According to recent reports, if you spent launch day watching reactions to GTA 6’s early hours roll in instead of playing, you might have walked away thinking that Rockstar made a chore simulator. That’s thanks to a few early missions that revolve around Jason getting his home ready for Lucia as she’s about to be released from prison. Players will paint a bedroom for her, fix a leaky roof, and repair some stairs. There’s also an optional quest where players can run errands to prepare for Lucia's arrival, like picking up groceries or buying her a necklace. All of this happens in the first few hours of the game. GTA 6 promptly ramps up after that, getting into the series’ usual flow of cop chases, heists, and shootouts. You can call it a slow start, but know that any mundane missions you’ve seen make up a very small amount of story that you’re likely to see in your very first play session.

The claim: GTA 6 doesn’t allow you to steal cars, or heavily restricts what you can steal.

According to recent reports, while there’s a grain of truth to this, it has been heavily exaggerated on social media. There are some select cars that you can’t steal in GTA 6, like those around Jason’s neighborhood or in an NPC’s car lot. But for the most part, you can jack just about any vehicle you see in Leonida. The catch is that you’ll need a device that can copy keys to get into some of the more expensive cars, and you won’t get that until Chapter 3. Being able to steal anything requires some patience as you play through the story, but be rest assured that you can do as much grand theft auto as ever in Grand Theft Auto.

The claim: Airplanes will bounce off of buildings instead of exploding on impact.

Recent findings suggest that this one is a little tricky to unpack because there seem to be two weird things colliding here. After videos of airplanes bouncing off of skyscrapers like rubber began to emerge on social media, players deduced that content creators were sharing videos where they had their Reduced Vehicle Damage setting turned on. It seemed like a textbook case of outrage farming, though there may be a slight bit of truth here. Some players have speculated that GTA 6 may have a few physics bugs that make it tough for certain airliners to blow up as expected. That may be an edge case, but I can confirm that I have crashed plenty of planes into buildings in GTA 6, and they have all exploded into a fiery wreck so far.

The claim: GTA 6 features no autosave, and you will lose progress if you don’t manually save.

In a recent development, when players started reporting that they were losing hours of gameplay because GTA 6 didn’t have an autosave feature, I was very confused. I can open my save file right now and see a dedicated auto save slot that is regularly refreshed as I play. I initially wrote it off as players either lying or not realizing that the auto save only triggers after completing major missions, but it turns out they weren’t hallucinating. GTA 6’s first patch fixed an concern where auto save wasn’t triggering properly. So, yes, GTA 6 does have autosave; it just wasn’t working correctly for some players at launch. It shouldn’t be a problem now, but always remember to save early and often just in case.

The claim: Lucia is cheating on Jason during the story.

This one is downright bizarre. One of the first talking points that came out about GTA 6 was that Jason is a “cuck” who does not realize that Lucia is cheating on him. As someone who has played through the story, I spent days trying to figure out where in the world that blatant lie could be coming from. It turns out it was a good old misinterpretation. Early in the story, Lucia sends a text to an unknown character, which she rushes to hide from Jason when he enters the scene. While some have interpreted that as Lucia having a secret lover, it actually turns out that she was texting a friend from prison. To players’ credit, the scene does feel like it’s built to make you think Lucia is hiding a big secret from Jason, so that reaction might have been exactly what Rockstar was hoping to provoke.

The claim: GTA 6 does not allow you to open fire and kill people in a gay club.

The ugliest rumor to come out of GTA 6 so far is that the game will not allow you to walk into a gay club in Vice City and kill people. There was even a clip going around social media that seemed to support that, sparking some grotesque reactions. The truth is that the location in the video isn’t specifically a gay club. It is a club, and it’s true that you can’t open fire in it, but that’s only because you can’t shoot inside any establishment in GTA 6. This claim would technically be true if there was a gay club in the game, but only as a side effect of the wider systems working the way they do. What is true, though, is that the game features an unkillable non-binary character, according to the actor who portrayed them.

#165835. Focker In-Law Review: Ben Stiller And Ariana Grande Bring Upcoming Laughs To An Old Franchise

Focker In-Law Review: Ben Stiller And Ariana Grande Bring Upcoming Laughs To An Old Franchise

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1156 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Slashfilm

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, there's an unwritten rule that states most comedy film franchises suffer from diminishing returns.
  • That mentioned, the "Meet the Parents" franchise is one that has quietly yet persistently endured over the past 26 years.
  • Given Hollywood's recent over-reliance on pre-existing IP, it wouldn't have been surprising to see such a movie be a lazy legacy sequel, milking the franchise for anything it had left (despite its lack of nipples).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, there's an unwritten rule that states most comedy film franchises suffer from diminishing returns. In general, it's hard to dispute that claim, as even several solid examples of funny comedy sequels tend to lack the freshness and originality of their predecessors. Thanks to this phenomenon, the existence of good comedy sequels, and especially good comedy franchises, feels almost unheard of.

That mentioned, the "Meet the Parents" franchise is one that has quietly yet persistently endured over the past 26 years. (Even longer than that, if you consider the fact that the 2000 film is in fact a remake of the hard-to-find 1992 original.) The initial film in the series, starring Ben Stiller as the hapless, unfortunately named Greg Focker, debuted early during the '00s "cringe comedy" trend, part of a wave of films and shows which delighted in the awkwardly relatable suffering of its protagonists. The family sitcom nature of the film helped lead to two more sequels, "Meet the Fockers" and "Little Fockers." The latter movie appeared to close out what was a trilogy for the last 16 years, until the release of "Focker In-Law" this month.

Given Hollywood's recent over-reliance on pre-existing IP, it wouldn't have been surprising to see such a movie be a lazy legacy sequel, milking the franchise for anything it had left (despite its lack of nipples). This is why the film is such a pleasant surprise, as it manages to recapture much of what made "Meet the Parents" hilarious without resorting to too many callback bits. Rather than merely flipping the first film's script and having the legacy cast pass the torch to younger characters, "Focker In-Law" impressively continues Greg's journey. Its a film whose cast and crew manage to find new laughs within an old franchise.

Sources indicate that being a legacy sequel, "Focker In-Law" naturally brings back as many of the characters seen throughout the prior movies as it can. In addition to Ben Stiller's Greg, his wife Pam (Teri Polo), her father Jack (Robert De Niro), his wife Dina (Blythe Danner), and even Pam's ex-fiancé Kevin (Owen Wilson) appear here. (Those hoping to see Greg's parents Bernie and Roz, played in the past by Barbara Streisand and Dustin Hoffman, are out of luck.).

In a recent development, thanks to the 16 year gap between sequels, Greg and Pam's children Henry and Samantha have grown up, and are now played by Skyler Gisondo and Beanie Feldstein, respectively. The plot is "Meet the Parents" in reverse; where that film saw Greg attempt to ingratiate himself with Jack before marrying Pam, now Henry is bringing home a woman he's hoping to marry: Olivia Jones (Ariana Grande).

In a recent development, it would've been easy for writer/director John Hamburg (who devised the story along with Ilana Glazer and Austen Earl) to pull a "The Force Awakens" on "Meet the Parents" and follow either Henry as he attempts to convince his dad and grandfather about his fiancé, or Olivia as she tries to win them over herself. Instead, Hamburg smartly keeps the focus on Greg's empty nest anxieties, allowing the franchise to grow older with him rather than try to pivot to a younger generation. It's a savvy choice, particularly because it doesn't require anyone to fill Stiller's shoes. After all, Stiller has not only perfected this character but also the comedic tone of the films. "Focker In-Law" contains some gags that would easily be over the top in the hands of someone less experienced, but Stiller can make Greg foolish while being sympathetic enough so things never go too far.

Industry observers note that there's no getting around the fact that "Focker In-Law" is a mainstream studio comedy sequel, and as such it does occasionally fall prey to some of the pitfalls of that genre. For one thing, it's not a particularly striking looking film. While that's on par with the rest of the franchise (which never seemed too interested in focusing on production design or cinematography), it's a shame that it mostly relies on a standardized aesthetic to be broadly appealing rather than going for something unique. The scourge of broadness does also crop up in some of the gags, including the moment where a series of mishaps causes Jack to be "baby birded" someone else's food at the dinner table, which is easily the most groan-worthy joke in the film.

That said, it's commendable that such a joke is the summit of the film's lowest common denominator, for the bulk of the set pieces are expertly constructed. A running joke about Jack's aggressive dog hating Greg escalates to a degree of chaos that's worthy of vintage John Hughes, something that's not easy to do given that writer's hugely influential status. In the same way John Hamburg could've given into temptation to make "Focker In-Law" a more conventional legacy sequel, he also could've fallen into the trap of making this sequel bigger and crazier.

In a recent development, instead, his history with the franchise means he innately understands that the films' bread and butter lies in steady escalation rather than sharp left turns. Ben Stiller can be set on fire and then almost frozen alive later, but such stunts wouldn't work if they weren't deployed correctly. Hamburg and organization know just how much and what type of track to lay for the train to reach the station.

The secret sauce of "Focker In-Law" is that it succeeds thanks to a thorough commitment to character. All the best comedy is character-based. While Ben Stiller's Greg is the film's centerpoint, the supporting characters are just as vital. Robert De Niro gives Jack a warmer demeanor this time around. Owen Wilson turns up Kevin's smarm to 11. Skyler Gisondo proves once again how deft a performer he can be, making Henry a comedic variant on his Decoy Dan from "Primetime," as he tries to be his own person while attempting to placate a father figure.

Ariana Grande has perhaps the hardest task in the movie, as her Olivia needs to walk the line between sweet girl next door and, in Greg's eyes, a master manipulator villainess. Her excellent performance allows the film to indulge in some broad tonal swings while keeping Olivia believable as a human rather than a caricature.

For folks whom "Meet the Parents" and its sequels were more excruciating experiences than hilarious comedies, "Focker In-Law" isn't going to change your mind. Yet for those of us who've related to Greg Focker's plight and foolish behavior over the years, the film is a little gift. It still has a broad relatability in its observations on family and relationships. Yet it's also refreshing in how it commits to following Greg on his never-ending journey to be a better person. Thanks to this commitment, "Focker In-Law" has given its franchise a upcoming lease on laughs.

"Focker In-Law" is in theaters on November 25, 2026.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • When we think of secrecy surrounding movies, naturally we think MCU, but the amount of secrecy that went into The Odyssey is insane.
  • It has been revealed that the actor portrays Odysseus's blind and devoted servant Eumaeus, a role that has been largely praised by critics.
  • I would go to lunch at Odeon, his favorite restaurant.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When we think of secrecy surrounding movies, naturally we think MCU, but the amount of secrecy that went into The Odyssey is insane. While I knew everything about it was kept under wraps, I didn’t realize just how much until I heard John Leguizamo’s story about landing the script, and it’s WILD.

It has been revealed that the actor portrays Odysseus's blind and devoted servant Eumaeus, a role that has been largely praised by critics. Turns out, Christopher Nolan knew exactly what he was doing when he cast Leguizamo in the part, and he didn’t even need to eat dessert first. The actor has previously gushed about working on the movie and the amazing shooting locations, but now he’s dishing to Kevin McCarthy on his On Film podcast about the Mission Impossible-level secret keeping that went into keeping the script under wraps:.

I would go to lunch at Odeon, his favorite restaurant. So we meet. He talks about the character. First of all, he talks about his career and everything. So that was just amazing to sit with him and hear him talk about his career was incredible. And then he claims, ‘I have this role for you. It's one of the most loyal characters in Western literature.’ And I was like, ‘Wow, that's a lot to live up to.’ He goes, ‘Yes.’ And I was like, ‘I'd love to do it if you'll have me.’ He offered me the role right there before dessert.

Industry observers note that leguizamo’s performance as Eumaeus has been called “sublime” by critics, and it’s easy to see why Nolan thought he was the right fit. Though the actor understands there’s a certain scene in the movie that earned him some hate for “the rest of cinema history,” and if you’ve seen it, then you know what he’s referring to. The actor didn’t even know the extent of his part until he got the script, which came to him as a top secret mission fit for James Bond:.

A week later after we close the deal. I have to be home at 12:00 on a Tuesday to receive the script. Nobody else can receive it. I have to receive it. Sign for it. And it comes in a blood red color that you can only see, you know, during a full solstice. [laughter] I don't know. It's impossible to see, dude. The black ink is shiny, and the red makes it so you can't copy it. But it's hard to read. It's really difficult to read.

It has been revealed that perhaps Marvel needs to take some notes from Nolan. While this seems like an insane level of secrecy for a book to screen adaptation, I admire the commitment to "no spoilers." Though the journalist asked the most crucial question, who delivered the script? Surely, FedEx wasn’t tasked with such a feat. Turns out one of Nolan’s personal assistants hand delivered it. However, there was still another step for him to be able to keep the confidential script:.

That's given to me, and I'm not allowed to share with anybody. My assistant had to sign an NDA.

The cloak and dagger seems to have worked as not even Tom Holland seems to have leaked anything. Additionally, Leguizamo shared that whenever Nolan made tweaks, the actor would have to turn in the old pages. This was definitely a first in his career, but one he feels was completely worth it, and I have to agree as the actor seemed to easily embody the role.

It’s not easy to bring an epic of this scale to life, and it was clear from the get-go that Nolan had a vision. Now that The Odyssey hit the 2026 movie schedule over the summer, the actor can focus on a different role. Though maybe one that doesn’t come with as much secrecy? Leguizamo will reprising his role as Sid the sloth in the upcoming 2027 movie, Ice Age: Boiling Point, which is set for a February 5, 2027 release.

Someone should ask him if he was given the Ice Age 6 script in red. Regardless, I’d love to hear his co-stars take on the spy antics it took to keep the script out of the wrong hands.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the upcoming "God of War" TV series is bringing back a very recognizable face from the smash-hit games that inspired it. In the latest significant bit of casting for the Prime Video adaptation, actor Deborah Ann Woll has been chosen to reprise her voice role as Faye (aka Laufey), the late wife of Kratos, who looms incredibly large throughout the events of both mainline games and the upcoming spin-off titled "God of War Laufey." The news comes straight from Sony Pictures Television and Amazon MGM Studios, with the official press release describing the character as:.

"The mysterious late wife of Kratos and mother of Atreus, Faye's abrupt passing sets in motion the events of 'God of War.' Along their journey, Kratos and Atreus discover secrets about Faye that make them wonder how well they truly knew her at all.".

Industry observers note that as gamers know, Faye's death prior to the events of the 2018 "God of War" game — the first in the more modern-generation games that shifted the action to Norse mythology — essentially kicked off the journey of Kratos and his young son Atreus as they discover hidden threats, newfound allies, and a much wider world than either character ever could've imagined. The "Daredevil" star now joins a packed cast that includes Dave Bautista as Kratos (taking over for original star Ryan Hurst, who injured himself during filming), Callum Vinson as Atreus, Mandy Patinkin as Odin, Ólafur Darri Ólafsson as Thor, Alastair Duncan as Mimir, and plenty more.

Look, if you can't beat your pitch-perfect casting from the first time around, then you might as well bring them back again. Deborah Ann Woll lent her voice and facial model to the character of Faye, starting with the 2018 "God of War" game, continuing with the highly-acclaimed sequel "Ragnarök," and soon taking on the lead role (yes, despite the inconvenience of Faye's death) in 2027's "God of War Laufey." Now, she's set to suit up in live-action for the Prime Video series, which is set to run for two full seasons as our next major video game adaptation.

This is both a strong vote of confidence in Woll's abilities as a performer (who most recently reprised her role as Karen Page in "Daredevil: Born Again") and an acknowledgement that, for certain characters, the original voice actor was simply the perfect choice all along. It's incredibly easy to imagine her bringing the same amount of pathos, tragedy, and bittersweet moments amid various flashbacks and visions that Kratos experiences throughout the saga ... and, perhaps, even in some original scenes further fleshing out their strong dynamic in the show. After all, when you have someone as talented and capable as Woll to work with, you might as well make full use of her time.

In a recent development, prime Video's "God of War" series comes from showrunner Ronald D. Moore, with "Shōgun" and "Fallout" director Frederick E.O. Toye helming the first two episodes of Season 1. After a brief pause following Ryan Hurst's injury and the subsequent recasting of Dave Bautista, the show is at the moment on track for a likely 2027 release. Stay tuned to /Film for more casting and production updates as they come in.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, sam's Club, Walmart, Amazon, and other retailers have been churning out early Black Friday deals since last week, so if you haven't been paying attention, you've already missed out on some good deals. But all hope is not lost: Costco recently started its own early sale, so you're still in time to find something you want at a low price. Below, I've rounded up my favorite tech deals from their sale—but keep in mind you'll need a membership to take advantage of these deals.

In a recent development, A powerful monitor with high-end specs can make gaming more immersive and greatly reduce input lag, which is helpful for any serious gamer looking for an edge over their opponents. The Samsung Odyssey G9 is a 49-inch gaming monitor with some impressive specs, including a 240Hz refresh rate and a 1 ms response time. It's available for $699.99 (originally $899.99), $200 off and the lowest price it has reached this year.

It has been revealed that if you're looking for a more premium (and far more massive) gaming monitor, the 57-inch Samsung Odyssey Neo G9, one of the best ultra-wide gaming monitors on the market, is right now on sale for $1,449.99 ($2,499.99 at launch). This monitor came out in 2023, earning an "excellent" review from PCMag for its impressive 7,680 x 2,160 4K resolution, its great color range and accuracy, a 240Hz refresh rate, 1,000 nits of brightness, and its overall design. To make full use of its powerful 240Hz refresh rate, you'll need to use DisplayPort 2.1, or you'll be limited to 120Hz. You'll also need a powerful graphics card. But if you have the right setup, this thing really delivers.

Recent findings suggest that the 15.3-inch Lenovo Legion is a powerful gaming laptop with premium specs, and with the current $600 discount, it's down to $1999.99 (originally $2,599.99). It has a powerful AMD Ryzen AI 9 processor, 32 GB of RAM, a GeForce RTX 5070 graphics card, and 1TB of SSD. PCMag gave the more affordable 5i version an excellent review for its price and performance, so if you have the cash for it, this one is even better.

According to recent reports, A soundbar is a great way to improve a home entertainment system without spending too much money. This 5.1 TCL Q6CH setup is currently $199.99 (originally $299.99), including a soundbar and subwoofer. This soundbar came out in 2024 and supports Dolby Atmos and DTS:X for that 3D sound, as well as AI Sonic, a tool that tunes your sound settings based on the setup of your room.

The latest AirPods Pro are a major step up from their previous generation. The third iteration of Apple's iconic earbuds deliver a number of quality-of-life and software improvements that make them worth the typical premium over the AirPods Pro 2—and right now, the AirPods Pro 3 are even cheaper than the previous generation: They're $179 at Costco (originally $249) in an early Black Friday deal.

The 15-inch MacBook Air is down to $1,249 (originally $1,499), the lowest price since Apple hiked prices this past summer. The M5 MacBook Air is the best laptop for most people looking for a new machine in 2026. In comparison to the already excellent M4 Air, the M5 base model has double the storage, and the powerful M5 chip makes the performance even smoother, according to Mashable's review. The aluminum design is as good as you'd expect from Apple's most popular portable laptop, and it includes a Liquid Retina display, Touch ID, a 12MP Center Stage Camera, and the Magic Keyboard.

The 15.6-inch Acer Aspire Go is a great value at its current $499.99 price (originally $699.99). The display is a touchscreen; it sports an AMD Ryzen 5 processor and it has 16GB of RAM and 1TB of storage. These aren't specs you normally find at this price, making it a great laptop for anyone looking to stretch their money as far as possible while getting a workhorse of a laptop.

I'm a fan of TCL TVs, and right now own the "non-pro" version of this TV. The 65-inch QM6K Pro is $599.99 (originally $999.99) and has the same internal hardware and Mini-LED panel as the regular QM6K, but it adds a CrystGlow anti-reflective coating that makes it more viewable in well-lit rooms and helps maintain a high picture contrast. The 144 Hz native refresh rate makes gaming smooth, and support for Dolby Vision IQ, HDR10+, HDR10, and HLG means you're well positioned to get the best sound quality when streaming movies or demonstrates.

Nowadays, both large retailers and small businesses compete for Black Friday shoppers, so you can expect practically every store to run sales through Monday, November 30, 2026. The “best” sales depend on your needs, but in general, the biggest discounts tend to come from larger retailers who can afford lower prices: think places like Amazon, Walmart, Target, Best Buy, and Home Depot. You can find all the best sales from major retailers on our Black Friday coverage.

Recent findings suggest that yes, Apple participates in Black Friday, though you may want to compare their sales with other retailers like Best Buy and Walmart. So far, the best Black Friday sale on an Apple product is the M5 MacBook Air on sale for $200 off, the lowest price since the price hike this summer.

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Buying a Google Pixel phone at launch is a waste of money, and the Pixel 11 Pro has proven to be no exception; after just three months on sale, the latest Pixel flagship has lost almost a third off its original price — hitting its lowest price so far.

It has been revealed that you can pick up the Pixel 11 Pro for $749 in Amazon's Black Friday sale. That's $350 off the usual price, and it all but wipes out the last few years of price hikes Google has been subjecting us to. The regular Pro isn't the only one getting that discount either, since the Pixel 11 Pro XL is $899 in Amazon's Black Friday sale. That's $400 off, and another all-time low for the largest Google phone of 2026.

Recent findings suggest that the Google Pixel 11 Pro was a little disappointing when it rolled out, especially if you were paying full price. But with $350 off? The apparent lack of meaningful upgrades isn't so bad. Especially since you do still get a brighter screen, HiLight, fresh AI features and better cameras.

Sources indicate that if you'd rather have a bigger screen and battery, the Pixel 11 Pro XL can be yours for $150 more. The benefits are basically the same, but if you need that extra real estate and longevity, this is probably the Pixel to get.

Sources indicate that one of my biggest gripes with the Google Pixel 11 Pro (and Pro XL) is that the upgrades you get over the Pixel 10 Pro are pretty minimal. So I resented that not only did Google charge full price for such a mediocre upgrade, but it also increased the price by $100. But with $350 off? That's basically the same price Pixel phones were three or four years ago, when they were considered a cheaper option — which is always a good thing.

In a recent development, so what are you actually getting for your money? The best thing about the standard Pixel 11 Pro is that it now comes with 256GB of storage as standard, which means you get double the space compared to the cheapest Pixel 10 Pro. On top of that, Google has improved the display on both sizes and turned up the screen brightness once again.

The best part of any new Google phone is the improvements to the cameras and AI performance. The ultrawide and telephoto lenses in particular benefit from larger sensors, improving the overall camera quality, and the AI enhancements mean that the new 120x zoom actually feels like magic.

Other AI-powered additions include the latest Magic Capture mode, which records video and pulls out the best stills as static photos. The new Rambler dictation mode is also significantly better than Google's old voice-to-text system, thanks to its ability to understand commands in a conversational way. I did experience some problems with this when I tested Rambler, so it is far from perfect.

Google also added a Live Translation feature which automatically converts any foreign language you hear on YouTube into your chosen tongue — in my case, English. There's also the customizable HiLight notification alert on the back, for those of you who tend to keep your devices face down.

Usual Pixel pitfalls still apply, though. Battery life could be better, and performance is appalling compared to rivals like Apple and Google. The base level of RAM has been reduced from 16GB to 12GB too, which means you'll need to buy the 1TB storage option to maximize the available memory.

Recent findings suggest that still, with prices dropping as far as this, grabbing the Pixel 11 Pro for $799 is well worth considering. It's not often a flagship device ends up this cheap, even if it isn't quite as powerful as rival flagships.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, "Avengers: Doomsday" is going to be one of the biggest movies of the year, if not ever, that much is certain.
  • Sources indicate that indeed, the worst thing one can say about this film right now is that it looks exactly like what you would expect.
  • Recent findings suggest that that being said, there is one notable reason to be excited about "Doomsday." No, not the X-Men (though their inclusion is certainly cool) or the return of Scarlet Witch (Elizabeth Olsen).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, "Avengers: Doomsday" is going to be one of the biggest movies of the year, if not ever, that much is certain. But so far, the movie's marketing has been quite, well, underwhelming. We already had one "Avengers" film (well, two) that relied entirely on gathering lots of known Marvel Cinematic Universe characters on screen at the same time. To do that again feels less special, as exciting as it is to see Cyclops (James Marsden) leading the X-Men into battle here.

Sources indicate that indeed, the worst thing one can say about this film right now is that it looks exactly like what you would expect. It's massive, sure, but it doesn't feel surprising in any way. Marvel announcing Robert Downey Jr. as Doctor Doom in the movie felt desperate, too, as it was obviously the studio's way of trying to win back the fans who'd been disappointed by the MCU's post-"Avengers: Endgame" output. "Spider-Man: Brand New Day" aside, Marvel's no longer the reliable hit machine that it once was.

Recent findings suggest that that being said, there is one notable reason to be excited about "Doomsday." No, not the X-Men (though their inclusion is certainly cool) or the return of Scarlet Witch (Elizabeth Olsen). Instead, it's the fact that "Doomsday" is technically a direct sequel to "Thunderbolts*," itself by far the best non-"Spider-Man" MCU movie since "Endgame." More specifically, it picks up where that film left off, with the titular team (also known as the West Chesapeake Valley Thunderbolts sponsored by Shane's Tire Tech giant) now officially being known as the Newly introduced Avengers.

Sure enough, the final "Doomsday" trailer features a few shots of the Newly introduced Avengers amidst all the new footage of Chris Evans as Steve Rogers, and it's enough to finally get me hyped for this film.

In a recent development, for the most part, the visuals in the final "Avengers: Doomsday" trailer look horrendously muted and dull, save for a single brief shot of David Harbour's Alexei Shostakov dressed in a horrendous New Avengers tracksuit staring in awe as Shang-Chi (Simu Liu) arrives at Avengers Tower. Immediately, the image both brightens the trailer and reminds you that as serious as "Doomsday" may be (with the old Avengers looking more tired and beaten up than ever), the New Avengers bring a whole different vibe to the table. After all, they're silly, not great at teamwork, and don't consider themselves to be gods. Instead, they talk through their psychological issues and even hug it out like something out of "Neon Genesis Evangelion.".

As the final trailer makes clear, "Doomsday" is all about different superhero groups coming together. You have the remnants of the original Avengers team, the X-Men, the Thunderbolts/New Avengers, and the Fantastic Four — plus the stragglers from various MCU titles that we collectively kind of forgot about. Each brings a different dynamic to the film, with the New Avengers specifically being a group of loser superheroes and criminals not unlike the Guardians of the Galaxy ... with the major difference being that the former have to save themselves before they can save anyone else. It's why "Thunderbolts*" makes for such an emotional gut punch, especially when its leads come together as a team, and the idea of seeing them interact with the MCU at large does more to make "Doomsday" feel interesting than any number of cameos could.

"Avengers: Doomsday" will see the New Avengers suit up alongside their companions when it hits theaters on December 18, 2026.

Of course, Bowen also has love for her other faux kids, Ariel Winter and Nolan Gould. In fact, Bowen gave them a shout out during a recent event, and she trolled them in a seriously mom-coded way that's hard not to love.

Bowen recently attended the 2026 Baby2Baby gala at the Pacific Design Center in West Hollywood, California, a non-profit she has been involved with for over 15 years. While there to raise money for children in poverty, Bowen was asked by Entertainment Tonight for her thoughts on Winter and Gould living together “almost like real-life brother and sister.” On that note, the Claire Dunphy actress didn't hold back her hilarious response:.

Screw them. Screw the two of you. They live so close to me, and I never see them. I run into them. I’m like, ‘What’s going on?!’.

This is sitcom-level irony, but this kind of fun tends to happen amongst the cast. For instance, Winter has playfully called out on-screen big sis Hyland for having a mini reunion without sending an invite to her and Gould. However, Bowen's comments are particularly funny, because they speak to the jokey but somewhat maternal relationship she has with her young co-stars.

It has been revealed that I can't see Hyland losing her “best fake daughter” title anytime soon due to Winter not sending an invite to her and Gould's new abode. However, in all seriousness, Bowen’s comment is all in good fun, and she went on to gush about Gould and Winter -- who played Luke and Alex Dunphy, respectively -- as well as their firm friendship:.

Recent findings suggest that I love them so much. I love that they live together. I love that they’re best friends. Everybody's like, ‘Are they together?’ I'm like, ‘No.’... They are roommates and best friends. They’re the best. I love them so much.

It has been revealed that not only are they NOT together, but it turns out that the best friend of your best friend makes for a good boyfriend. Winter is at the moment dating Gould’s best friend, after being introduced to him by her TV bro. Given she keeps her private life mostly out of public eye, she hasn’t revealed many details about the relationship. I'd imagine her former co-stars are update to date, though, as Bowen previously shared that their close bond is why the cast has remained on such friendly terms.

Sources indicate that given Bowen literally watched the younger cast members grow up, it’s understandable that she would have a motherly relationship with them… right down to the A+ mom jokes. As for possibly hanging out with them, Bowen also shared this quip:.

Hit me up, Ariel and Nolan. Come on. Mommy needs you.

It's a moment like this that makes me wish a Modern Family revival of sorts would happen at some point. The cast's chemistry was just too perfect, and they clearly continue to have that bond off camera. I'm not sure whether ABC would be interested in such a production, but I'll keep my fingers crossed that it happens.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

For now, though, it’s lovely to know that Julie Bowen is thinking about her on-screen kids… and (playfully) calling them out. It's a moment that feels like it's almost straight out of Modern Family, and If you don’t believe me, you can watch every zany family moment from all 11 seasons using a Disney+ subscription.

Also, let’s hope Winter and Gould get the message and hit up Bowen for lunch pronto!

GTA 6 Is So Unstoppable It's Even Made Nickelback Go Viral

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that it's still a debate whether Grand Theft Auto 6 has the best gaming soundtrack of 2026, but it certainly has the most soundtrack of 2026.
  • Thanks to GTA 6, Nickelback's 2001 angst ballad "How You Remind Me" has been getting a lot of play — kind of.
  • You might be somewhat surprised to hear "How You Remind Me" making the rounds again, years removed from its days reigning over the Billboard charts.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that it's still a debate whether Grand Theft Auto 6 has the best gaming soundtrack of 2026, but it certainly has the most soundtrack of 2026. Rockstar Games' latest open-world crime epic features more than 800 songs, most of which you'll hear on its 26 genre-themed radio stations. Of all this breadth of wild music, you'd figure the most popular song on the soundtrack would be something that had overlap with a Fast and Furious OST. But it turns out the single best song in the GTA 6 soundtrack is something by... Nickelback?

Thanks to GTA 6, Nickelback's 2001 angst ballad "How You Remind Me" has been getting a lot of play — kind of. Technically, this version is a cover. GTA 6's Kaleidoscope FM radio station plays alternate-language versions of popular songs, the indisputable best of which is "Ola Afta Poui Fovamai," by the Greek singer and alternate former tourism minister Alkistis Protopsalti. As far as covers go, this is one for the ages. Seriously, listen:.

You might be somewhat surprised to hear "How You Remind Me" making the rounds again, years removed from its days reigning over the Billboard charts. To this day, the most-played radio song of the 2000s has been relegated to background music in the daddest bars from Mississauga to Massapequa. It is arguably the epitome not just of Dad Rock but specifically of Divorced Dad Rock. If "How You Remind Me" was a person, its kitchen would include Slim Jims (assorted flavors), cold pizza (definitely pepperoni), and nothing else. It would drive a 2014 Corvette Stingray (bright red, obviously). It would live on the golf course.

But with "Ola Afta Poui Fovamai," Protopsalti injects a youthful, upbeat verve to Chad Kroeger's genius composition that legendarily emerged, nearly fully formed, from his brain in just 45 minutes following an argument with a partner. It's the sort of track you'd play in a convertible on a sunny day, or in the bathroom while getting ready for a party themed after The Devil Wears Prada (the good one). There is practically zero Divorced Dad energy in "Ola Afta Poui Fovamai." It is transformational.

Recent findings suggest that I am far from the only person to completely lose my shit over the resurfacing of a song that hit number-one on charts in Austria, Canada, Denmark, Ireland, and the United Kingdom, in addition to peaking in the top ten in various other international markets. As of this writing, searches for "Nickelback" on Bluesky are all about "Ola Afta Poui Fovamai." On Facebook, Greek culture accounts are sharing the cover as a point of national pride. When Canadian streamer Dan "Greenskull" Hammill heard it for the first time in-game, he burst into a karaoke rendition that has since gone semi-viral.

It has been revealed that truth told, the Canadian rock quartet legitimately is one of my guilty pleasures. As a teenager, I once suffered a pretty serious concussion in a skiing accident; according to the paramedics, I spent the entire ride to the hospital singing "Photograph" in my unconscious state. Mortifying, but also hard to deny. Such is the allure of GTA 6. In being a mirror of our world, it's also a mirror of our lives, thus revealing truths we may not have otherwise been ready to admit. The boyfriends of the world start doing more chores for their partners. Those of us who've let the gym routine fall by the wayside pick it back up again. Nickelback? A guilty pleasure? I no longer see anything to be guilty about here.
