📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (609 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Slashfilm

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Earlier this year, Steven Spielberg announced that his next movie as a director would be a Western.
  • In a recent development, now, Deadline has revealed that the movie, an adaptation of Kevin Barry's novel "The Heart in Winter," will star Cillian Murphy, Jessie Buckley and Mark Rylance, and it's hard not to be elated.
  • In a recent development, no one's more enthused than Spielberg, though.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Earlier this year, Steven Spielberg announced that his next movie as a director would be a Western. This will be his first official crack at the most American of film genres, and that's reason enough for cinephiles to get excited.

In a recent development, now, Deadline has revealed that the movie, an adaptation of Kevin Barry's novel "The Heart in Winter," will star Cillian Murphy, Jessie Buckley and Mark Rylance, and it's hard not to be elated. Factor in that Barry's book is being adapted into a script by Oscar-winner Paul Thomas Anderson, and there isn't a word in the English language to capture the utter exhilaration movie fans are feeling at this moment.

In a recent development, no one's more enthused than Spielberg, though. As he told Deadline:.

"It's really the excitement for me to get to work together with my dear friend and colleague Paul Thomas Anderson on a genre, but more particularly, the genre notwithstanding, a story that quite quickly became close to both our hearts and we felt that we could do as a team.".

Murphy will play Tom Rourke, an Irish immigrant eking out a living in Butte, Montana. He works as an assistant to a photographer and supplements his income by penning letters for illiterate miners seeking potential brides from the east. He needs the extra scratch, too, due to his alcohol and opium addictions. Tom is spiritually adrift until mail-order bride Polly Gillespie arrives in Butte. They fall fast in love, steal some money, and set what proves to be an eventful course for San Francisco.

Industry observers note that overall, Barry's book has echoes of Spielberg's theatrical directing debut on "The Sugarland Express," as it's about two lovers on the run from the law. But this being the late 1800s, and the pair being challenged as horseback riders, their journey isn't quite as fast-paced.

Sources indicate that kevin Barry's "The Heart in Winter" has been described as "a tragedy written as farce" (per The Guardian). Critics found it hilarious and wildly entertaining, and after his excellent work on "One Battle After Another," I can't imagine anyone more suited to a tale about a character with an opium addiction stealing a mail-order bride and heading to San Francisco than Paul Thomas Anderson. But what's most interesting to me is that this will be the first time Anderson has written an entire script for another filmmaker. He previously did rewrites on the Apple-backed "Killers of the Flower Moon" and "Napoleon" for Martin Scorsese and Ridley Scott, but he's the primary writer here.

Sources indicate that as for Steven Spielberg, no filmmaker alive knows more about Western conventions than him, and you can rest assured he will aggressively avoid cliché. I mean, he'll be sure to keep the horizon line out of the middle of the frame, lest John Ford's eye-patched ghost haunt him for the rest of his days, but don't expect traditional Western violence of the shootout and saloon brawl variety. I haven't read the book yet, so I don't know if such scenes exist in Barry's novel, but if they do, they'll look unlike any shootout or brawl you've ever seen.

What's curious is that Spielberg went with the Montana-set "The Heart in Winter," given that he'd been talking about making a Texas Western. Texas is not Montana by a long shot, which makes me wonder if he might change the location of Barry's novel. I doubt he'd do that, so now he's cheesed off everyone in Texas who was hoping he'd make their state look sensationally epic. He'll have to make it up to them somehow.

James Gunn's DC Exit Has People Asking About Keanu Reeves And Constantine Again (& I Don’t Hate It)

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (742 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cinemablend

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that with James Gunn and Peter Safran’s exiting DC, it's unknown if the DCU will continue or if we can expect yet another reboot.
  • A Constantine sequel has technically been "in the works" since 2022, and at the time, it was reported that writer Akiva Goldsman was working on the script.
  • Sources indicate that well, I’ll tell you this.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that with James Gunn and Peter Safran’s exiting DC, it's unknown if the DCU will continue or if we can expect yet another reboot. However, with one chapter closing for the studio, the start of a new might mean some long-gestating projects could get a second chance. Amid the corporate change, people have been asking about Keanu Reeves' long-discussed Constantine sequel again, and honestly, I don’t hate the possibility of seeing the 2005 movie finally get a follow-up.

A Constantine sequel has technically been "in the works" since 2022, and at the time, it was reported that writer Akiva Goldsman was working on the script. Director Francis Lawrence has been committed making another flick centered on Reeves' DC character, and he previously confirmed the leading man was "excited" about the idea. While there was a positive update in 2025, news has been scarce since then. Yet, when the director spoke with Collider about Sunrise on the Reaping, he gave John Constantine fans some hope:.

Sources indicate that well, I’ll tell you this. Not that I want anybody to lose their jobs, so this is not like a schadenfreude kind of thing, but I will say that we’ve been trying to make Constantine 2 for 20-something years, and we have an idea, and we have a script, and we’ve been wanting to make it, and the people that were at DC were an impediment to us making it. So, we are now more hopeful as of yesterday’s news that maybe now there will be another opportunity.

This is sure to be music to some fans' ears amid the major corporate shift. Jeremy Latcham, a Marvel Studios alum who worked with Gunn on Guardians of the Galaxy, is stepping into the role of DC Studios CEO. As a result, Gunn’s DC universe might be over, and Lawrence -- who's sympathetic to the exiting CEOs -- seems to be confident that this could open the door for a Constantine sequel.

Sources indicate that of course, Lawrence is also upfront about having no idea what the studio has planned. For all he knows, they could want a different John Constantine for a shared universe. With that in mind, he’s also perfectly fine if the studio want to do a new take and allows him to make a sequel to HIS version with Reeves. In Lawrence's mind, two iterations can co-exist.

At this point, Francis Lawrence has made it clear that the project is further along than fans think, as they have a script ready to go. The only obstacle in his way is a thumbs up from the powers that be:.

Industry observers note that but again, we’ve been trying to make this for 20-something years, and there’s always been obstacles in the road to making it, and it’s not me, it’s not Keanu, it’s not Akiva. J.J. [Abrams] is on it, as well. We all want to do it. So, it’s really going to be people at Paramount, Warner, whoever’s running DC now, getting everybody on board to say, like, 'Hey, we can do a sequel of our version of Constantine.'.

Recent findings suggest that 2005's Constantine has earned quite the cult following. Believe it or not, Reeves wasn’t fans' first pick for the role, and that's because of how much of a departure from the comics his take on John is. The character has lived on in the live-action space since then, with Matt Ryan taking on the trench coat in 2014 for a short-lived NBC show. Ryan continued to portray Constantine in The CW’s Arrowverse and voiced the DC antihero in various animated works through 2024.

In a recent development, however, a portion of fans still seem hopeful that Keanu Reeves will get another chance to play the character, and I’d love to see him back in the role. Considering Reeves' skills as an actor and his love for John, I have no doubt he can slide right back into the role. We'll have to play the waiting game on that front, though, as DC Studios has yet to reveal any new plans that will follow James Gunn and Peter Safran's departures.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

In the meantime, stream Francis Lawrence's Constantine using an HBO Max subscription.

#165820. 5 Reasons Why The Hunger Games: Sunrise On The Reaping Ruled The Box Office

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1627 w)

General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Slashfilm ↗ Open Full Page

5 Reasons Why The Hunger Games: Sunrise On The Reaping Ruled The Box Office

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1627 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Slashfilm

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, the biggest YA franchise in the game is back on top.
  • Sources indicate that directed once again by franchise shepherd Franchise Lawrence, "Sunrise on the Reaping" opened to a massive $120 million domestically.
  • "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" looked like it was going to be a bigger hit than people realized, which proved true.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the biggest YA franchise in the game is back on top. Lionsgate released "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" in theaters over the weekend, and to say that the franchise's latest prequel film did well would be an understatement. This movie is already a huge hit for the studio and has brought the property back to its former, $100 million-plus opening weekend glory.

Sources indicate that directed once again by franchise shepherd Franchise Lawrence, "Sunrise on the Reaping" opened to a massive $120 million domestically. Internationally, the prequel bowed to $105 million, giving it a gigantic $225 million global start. It's now Lionsgate's biggest opening of 2026 overall. "Michael" ruled the box office with a $218 million global opening earlier this year, but "Sunrise on the Reaping" even managed to best the King of Pop. Now, whether or not this movie gets to the $1 billion mark like "Michael" in the long run is another question entirely, but it illustrates just how significant this opening was.

"The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" looked like it was going to be a bigger hit than people realized, which proved true. It arrived right in line with bullish estimates, which climbed through the roof in the weeks leading up to its arrival. As such, it's now poised to become one of the biggest hits of the year overall.

So, what went right here? How did Lionsgate manage to make such a massive bet and have it pay off so spectacularly well? We're going to look at the biggest reasons why "Sunrise on the Reaping" ruled the box office on its opening weekend. Let's get into it.

Recent findings suggest that the biggest thing that this movie had going for it is that it wasn't just another "Hunger Games" film or a prequel for the sake of a prequel. It was a story that hardcore fans of the franchise have been waiting a long time to see. Specifically, one involving the famed games where Haymitch Abernathy, the character played by Woody Harrelson in the previous "Hunger Games" movies, won.

"Sunrise on the Reaping" pits a young Haymitch (Joseph Zada) against President Snow (Ralph Fiennes), to put it in the simplest possible terms. "Hunger Games" author Suzanne Collins wrote the book the movie is based on and, rather crucially, the novel was received very well by fans. And by most accounts, Francis Lawrence, with the help of Collins, delivered one heck of an adaptation. All of this to say, the movie promised something fans had been wanting for a hot minute and delivered the goods when the time arrived.

Beyond that, Jennifer Lawrence also broke her silence on her "Hunger Games" return in "Sunrise on the Reaping" ahead of the film's release, assuring that this movie was getting the original gang back together. That undoubtedly helped get more casual viewers on board who perhaps were only more interested in the original set of "Hunger Games" films. Overall, Lionsgate made the most of what this story had to offer, turning it into not just another movie but a true event within one of the biggest franchises of the last 20 years — one that demanded to be seen on the biggest screen available as soon as possible.

Recent findings suggest that this is the kind of movie that hardcore fans were always going to be in the bag for, no matter what. That having been said, positive word of mouth never hurts. And while critics were, more or less, on this film's side, it worked like gangbusters for the intended audience. In the case of a long-running, beloved franchise, that is always more crucial.

"The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" holds a decent 69% critical approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, as of this writing. However, it carries a stellar 94% audience score, which is near-universal praise from actual ticket buying fans. It also earned a damn good A- CinemaScore, which means word of mouth is going to be great in the weeks to come. Even though "Focker In-Law" could be a rare comedy box office hit over Thanksgiving, with Disney's "Hexed" opening as well, there should be more than enough room for this prequel to have a stellar second frame over the holiday weekend.

/Film's Nina Starner wrote that "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" is a prequel that "delivers" in her review. Certain critics may have been a bit softer on it, but enough of them liked it to prevent the needle from being pushed down. More importantly, fans are loudly proclaiming their love for this film, which is going to do way more to motivate viewers who might have been on the fence to check it out in the coming weeks.

Sources indicate that lionsgate doesn't always have a lot of success when playing in the big-budget realm, but this franchise has generally been the exception to that rule. All of "The Hunger Games" movies have been hits at the box office and, save for the very first film, they've all benefited from November releases. This ended up being an "if it ain't broke, don't fix it" situation. All the same, the studio wisely picked the perfect spot on the calendar for this prequel to thrive.

In a recent development, word of mouth can't be predicted, but getting in on an otherwise fairly dead pre-Thanksgiving weekend was very wise. "Sunrise on the Reaping" got one totally unimpeded weekend to do its thing and will now benefit from a long, five-day holiday weekend over Thanksgiving. It's basically going to have nine full days of ruling the box office before taking any sort of meaningful hit.

"The Hunger Games: Mockingjay — Part 2" ruled the box office in 2015, also in November, delivering a $102 million opening weekend en route to $653 million worldwide. This latest prequel had an even bigger opening, meaning it could eclipse that global figure when all's said and done. Not to get too ahead of ourselves, but it may wind up closer to "Mockingjay — Part 1" ($766 million worldwide), if all goes well.

Wherever the chips fall at the end of the day, it's going to be in large part because this movie wasn't competing with a slew of other blockbusters in the midst of a crowded summer. This is the big cinematic event of choice right now and will be for at least a couple of weeks.

According to recent reports, it certainly doesn't happen too often, but if a franchise gets it right, the breakout sequel effect can come into play. One of the best examples in history is "The Dark Knight." While Christopher Nolan's "Batman Begins" was actually a bit of a box office disappointment, pulling in a so-so $373 million worldwide, "The Dark Knight" was simply too good to be ignored and made $1 billion at a time when movies rarely ever hit that milestone.

Other examples include "John Wick"/"John Wick: Chapter 2" and "Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse/"Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse." A very good first movie happened, people caught up with it after the fact, and that resulted in a much larger audience for the sequel. That brings us back to "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping." Despite being the sixth entry in this property, it benefited like a breakout sequel would have.

Recent findings suggest that 2023's "The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes" was a surprise victor at the Thanksgiving box office, ultimately pulling in nearly $350 million worldwide on a $100 million budget. A solid result, but it wasn't nearly what the first four movies in the "Hunger Games" franchise made. However, audiences and fans caught up with it and ended up enjoying it. So, after an eight-year break, Lionsgate kind of used that first prequel to prime the pumps on this franchise, even if that wasn't the intention.

The end result is that "Songbirds & Snakes" teed up the ball for "Sunrise on the Reaping," paving the way for the film to enjoy a much, much bigger opening than its predecessor. It's not a traditional breakout sequel, but it's a breakout sequel to a prequel people enjoyed.

Recent findings suggest that perhaps the most important factor when it comes to playing Monday morning quarterback with the success of "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" has to do with how significant franchises are typically handled in Hollywood these days. Spin-offs. TV reveals. Animated entries. Theme parks. More merchandise than anyone knows what to do with.

According to recent reports, that never really happened with "The Hunger Games." That's in no small part because author Suzanne Collins has a lot of say over how those affairs are handled. Even so, there was an eight-year gap between movies by the time "The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes" came around and another three years before "Sunrise on the Reaping." Neither Lionsgate nor Collins ever allowed for overexposure to get the best of this franchise. That allowed for people to be legitimately excited about this film.

Former Disney CEO Bob Iger even admitted that multiple Marvel shows and Pixar movies going to streaming hurt those brands. The Marvel Cinematic Universe is mighty, but even fans grew tired of that. Likewise, Pixar is as good as cinema gets, yet audiences learned that they could just watch those movies at home. Meanwhile, Lionsgate has maintained discipline with the "Hunger Games" films and ensured that they remained cinematic events. Short-term gains and overdoing it would have potentially kneecapped what is now one of the studio's biggest hits in years. Hollywood could stand to learn a thing or two from this sort of execution.

"The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" is in theaters now.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Prince William is reportedly actively considering a blueprint for a “far-reaching restructuring” of the British monarchy, which he would implement once he ascends to the throne. His brother, Prince Harry, would be at the forefront of these changes: The future monarch reportedly wants only active members of the royal family who carry out duties on his behalf to retain their royal titles and the style of “Royal Highness.” These titles would therefore no longer be an “automatic privilege of birth” but would instead be equivalent to a “job title.”.

Industry observers note that the initiative was detailed by Tom Sykes, a journalist and writer specializing in the royals, in his book Dukes of Hazard, to be published next February, excerpts of which were published by the Mail on Sunday on Saturday, November 21. The author, “a royal authority with impeccable society contacts” as the newspaper puts it, is said to have obtained confessions from friends of Prince William.

“If you are a working royal—going out, touring the country, doing diplomatic work, doing government work, having a public role, pressing the flesh, getting out of bed on a wet Wednesday to go to Sheffield—then you will be an HRH and you will have a prince or princess title. You will also get an allowance, a salary, and a place to live. One place to live,” the associate of the prince explained to Sykes. “If you are not doing those things and you are not a working royal, you will not get to be an HRH, you will not get a free or subsidized place to live, and you will not get any special favors. You will, however, be a private citizen free to get on with your life and make money any way you choose.”.

Industry observers note that by implementing this measure, Prince William hopes to prevent potential media scandals regarding the legitimacy of certain individuals’ right to retain their titles if they are not prominent members of the Firm (Prince Harry) or if they are under legal scrutiny (Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor). But also, and above all, the Prince of Wales hopes to offer an option to his children, Princess Charlotte, 11, and Prince Louis, eight, who could easily renounce their titles to pursue independent careers. The question does not arise for the eldest child of the Prince and Princess of Wales, Prince George, 13, whose future as heir to the throne is “guaranteed.” In fact, none of the three use their royal titles, preferring simply to be called by their first names and the surname Wales.

In a recent development, under the rules established by King George V in 1917, the title of prince or princess, along with the predicate, is granted at birth to the sovereign’s children and to the children of the sovereign’s sons, as well as to all the children of the Prince of Wales’s eldest son. Prince William’s children, therefore, received these titles at birth, while Prince Harry’s children, Archie and Lilibet (ages seven and five), did not become prince and princess until King Charles III ascended the throne.

They may have to give them up if Prince William carries out his proposal. “Under William’s current plan, the prince and princess titles of Harry and Meghan’s children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet, would be legally removed, along with the royal styles and princely titles of Harry and Meghan themselves,” writes Tom Sykes in his book. To do so, according to Sykes’s book, constitutional advisers have told William that he could problem letters patent, an official document authorized by the king. Such a decision could strain the relationship between the two brothers.

Sykes is convinced that Prince William would garner the approval of his subjects and “enormous public support in a country increasingly impatient with the cost and perceived excess of a sprawling royal household,” according to those close to him.

In October 2025, Prince William confided to actor Eugene Levy—whom he was hosting at Windsor Castle for the taping of Levy’s show The Reluctant Traveler—that “there are points when you look at tradition and go, Is that still fit for purpose today? Is that still the right thing to do? Are we still doing and having the most impact we could be having?”.

Kensington Palace, however, declined to comment on the rumor. “As a matter of policy, we don’t comment on books or claims made within them.”.

Saatva is renowned for making some of the best mattresses on the market for a luxurious sleep experience. And I should know, I've tested several of them. Which is why I was looking forward to trying out the Saatva Graphite Memory Foam Pillow, a pillow the brand recommends to hot sleepers in all sleep positions. Disappointingly, the reality didn't live up to the expectation.

Type: Memory foam and latexBest for: Combination sleepersSizes: standard and high loftTrial: 45 nightsWarranty: 1-yearPrice: $165 at Saatva.

As the name suggests, the Graphite Memory Foam Pillow is made with mostly memory foam with a little bit of shredded natural latex thrown into the mix. It has a different design to any of the best pillows I've tested before — a thin shredded latex core, sandwiched by two slabs of graphite-infused memory foam for, apparently, improved breathability (spoiler: this was not my experience).

Industry observers note that I tested a queen-size Graphite Memory Foam Pillow in standard loft, but it's also available in a high loft. The surface is on the firmer side and, thanks to its memory foam construction, offers a little contouring. Although I prefer a plusher feel, the surface isn’t what makes this pillow uncomfortable. It was how the bottom edge of the pillow seemed to squish flat, causing my neck to sit at an unnatural angle, or my head to slide off — depending on which position I was sleeping in.

It has been revealed that another massive drawback had to do with the temperature regulation. Despite testing during November when my house was cool at night, I woke up to warm spots on the pillow.

If you've read enough and want a quick signpost to a more comfortable alternative, check out my review of the Saatva Cloud Memory Foam Pillow (I rated it 4.5/5).But if you're still wondering if the Saatva Graphite Memory Foam pillow could be the right fit for you, strap yourself in for my full review below.

Saatva is a premium mattress brand, and that’s reflected in the price of their pillows too. The Graphite Memory Foam Pillow has an MSRP price of $165 for a standard loft, queen size pillow. Bedding and accessories aren't included in the current Saatva Black Friday sale. However, you do stand to save $40 when you buy as part of a Sateen Sheet Set bundle.

In my opinion, the $165 price tag is steep, especially considering how much of the pillow is comprised of memory foam and there are no certifications for the organic cotton cover or the natural latex.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

A 45-night trial is a bit longer than other brands, however, a 1-year warranty is on the low end for a premium-priced pillow.

Sources indicate that the Saatva Graphite Memory Foam Pillow is available in two different lofts and costs $165. While regular Saatva mattress sales shave hundreds off of the best Saatva mattresses during major sale events, pillows and bedding aren't included in those discounts as standalone products. This pillow includes 45 night sleep trial, 1-year warranty and free shipping.

In a recent development, like many of the best pillows we've tested, there’s a lot more going on with the design of this pillow than appears from the outside. It’s sold in a standard (4-5" tall) or high loft (6-7" tall), with the high loft more suitable to broader bodies.

Recent findings suggest that the pillow effectively has three main layers, starting with a removeable knit cotton cover. Below the cotton cover is an 'inner pillow.' Two medium-thick blocks of memory foam infused with graphite are placed on the front and the back sides of the inner pillow. Memory foam is not a breathable foam, so graphite is used to promote a cool night’s sleep.

Between the memory foam blocks is a bag that contains shredded natural latex and memory foam. It’s quite thin and can be removed entirely from the inner pillow if need be. However, you can’t open that core to add or remove the shredded foams.

Lastly, the memory foam has a CertiPUR-US certification. Although Saatva say the cover is made with organic cotton and they include natural latex in the pillow, no other certifications are provided that verify this.

After one week of testing, here’s what I can tell you about the Saatva Graphite Memory Foam Pillow’s comfort and temperature regulation.

It has been revealed that the Saatva Graphite Memory Foam Pillow arrived in a plastic bag within a cardboard box. It was already fully expanded, so I was able to take it out of the bag and sleep on it right away. Unfortunately, I noticed off gassing from this pillow right away, and even more so when I slept on the pillow. As someone with a sensitive nose, I tried to sleep on my back, so I wouldn’t have to smell the pillow.

A week before I tested Saatva’s Graphite Memory Foam Pillow, I tested the Saatva Cloud Memory Foam Pillow. I’m not a huge fan of memory foam but I found the Saatva Cloud Memory Foam Pillow to be extremely comfortable. Unfortunately, I couldn’t say the same of the Saatva Graphite Memory Foam Pillow.

According to recent reports, I ordered it in the standard loft size which, according to its dimensions, should have been the perfect size to allow me to sleep on my back, stomach, and side. However, it didn’t matter which way I slept, I couldn’t find any position that was particularly comfortable. And there is a single reason why.

It has been revealed that when I laid my head down, it didn’t sink into the pillow very much. There was some slight contouring. But at the same time, the bottom length of the pillow (near my shoulders), flattened down creating a significant angle that offered no support to my neck or shoulders. I tried to move the inner shredded latex and memory foam core to prevent this flattening, but nothing seemed to work.

According to recent reports, if I slept on my stomach, my head would slide off the pillow. On my side or my back? My neck would feel strained. Because the bottom had flattened out, my neck was not being held up and thus would dip down at an odd angle. If I was lying on my back, my head would be pushed forward more – which wasn’t comfortable. On my side, I was having to hold my head in place or put my hand under the bottom of the pillow to sort of fluff it up.

All in all, I did not sleep well on this pillow during testing.

Recent findings suggest that bedding brands have long claimed that infusing graphite into memory foam can offer significant cooling properties. I haven’t ever experienced such a thing, not with Saatva’s Graphite Memory Foam Topper and not with this Graphite Memory Foam Pillow.

I didn’t wake up hot and sweaty when sleeping on this pillow. However, I would wake up and notice warm spots around my head. This was odd considering I tested the pillow in November when my home dropped to the 60s at night. I used a breathable Quince linen pillowcase during this time, too.

I think the lack of breathability in this pillow has a lot to do with the design, in particular, those two blocks of memory foam on the front and back of the pillow. Memory foam doesn’t allow for much air to flow through and dissipate heat.

According to recent reports, most pillows should be replaced after two years. However, if you notice the loft breaking down quicker or your pillow having trouble bouncing back if you fold it in half, you should replace it as soon as possible.

Sources indicate that I only slept on the Graphite Memory Foam Pillow for one week, and in that time, I haven’t noticed any signs of sagging or breakdown. Saatva include high-quality, premium materials in their products and estimates longer lifespans for their bedding, so I’m sure you don’t have to worry about this pillow breaking down rapidly. That said, the one-year warranty is on the low end of warranties for premium pillow brands.

The cotton cover of the Graphite Memory Foam Pillow is removeable and can be thrown in the wash. Machine wash it on cold with a delicate cycle then tumble dry the cover on low or hang it to dry.

According to recent reports, remember, to wash the cover on occasion as it can absorb sweat stains, facial cream, or even saliva. This will help extend the lifespan of your pillow. If you notice that anything has bled through to the inner pillow, you can spot clean it as needed.

Usually when I test a pillow, there’s at least one type of sleeper I can suggest the pillow to – but that’s not the case with the Saatva Graphite Memory Foam Pillow. Not only does it sleep warm at night, but the design of the pillow resulted in a variety of challenges for my neck or head no matter if I was sleeping on my side, stomach, or back.

In a recent development, the materials aren’t certified organic or completely non-toxic and you can only wash the cover. At least you get the chance to order it in standard or high loft. Considering all the flaws, the price doesn’t feel worth it, even with a 45-night trial with free returns.

I hate to say this about a Saatva product, but they have plenty of others like the Saatva Down Alternative Pillow or the Cloud Memory Foam Pillow that are far more comfortable and/or worth their price.

✅ You're a stomach sleeper with a small build: The pillow flattens considerably along the bottom edge, so it is easier (albeit, not particularly comfortable) to lay your head on the pillow when sleeping on your stomach. Just be mindful that your head might slip off as the pillow doesn’t always provide enough contouring or sink in to prevent such a thing.

✅ You want a pillow with a removeable cover: Thankfully, you can remove the cotton cover of this pillow and easily throw it into the wash.

✅ You want 45 days to try it out: Most pillows come with a 30-day trial, but Saatva allows you to try this pillow for 45 days and will offer a full refund and free return if it’s not to your liking.

Sources indicate that ❌ You sleep hot: I experienced warm spots when sleeping on this pillow at night – and that’s coming from someone who doesn’t sleep hot. Notably, testing was done in late fall when the evenings were particularly cool in my house.

❌ You like more of a sink in feel to your pillow: While the Graphite Memory Foam Pillow offers a bit of contouring, your head won’t sink in that much. It’s better described as having a firm surface.

❌ You want more neck support: The bottom edge of the pillow flattens which doesn’t offer as much neck support for side sleepers. It also means that when you’re sleeping on your back, it pushes your head forward and creates tension in your neck.

In a recent development, where the Graphite Memory Foam Pillow has a shredded foam core, the Saatva Cloud Memory Foam Pillow’s entire inner filling is comprised of shredded latex and memory foam. This results in a far more comfortable and supportive feel and superb temperature regulation. Best yet? The Cloud Memory Foam is $30 cheaper making it a far better buy.

Recent findings suggest that if you prefer a cleaner or non-toxic night of sleep, consider the Birch Organic Pillow as it is made with shredded latex foams within a layer of wool padding. You’ll experience a cooler night’s sleep on this pillow that starts out with a $149 (originally $198) price tag. However, if you’re a stomach or side sleeper with wide shoulders, it may not be the best option.

In a recent development, the Purple GridCloud Pillow features the brand’s signature Gelflex grid as well as a microfiber fill resulting in a luxury plush feel and a pillow that does not flatten. Despite its lack of size, firmness, or loft options, the Purple GridCloud Pillow has great temperature regulation and is ideal for side and back sleepers. Even the $149 price is more affordable than the Saatva Graphite Memory Foam pillow.

It will also surely be one of their most profitable, given the hype around this movie. Despite Marvel Studios' well-publicized troubles of late, the Avengers' return remains highly anticipated. As such, any new revelations Marvel is willing to provide about the team-up movie are significant to say the least.

In a recent development, the final "Doomsday" trailer doesn't actually feature any major reveals, which is a good thing for those who prefer to keep their theater experience as pure as possible. For those who like to know as much as they can ahead of a Marvel Cinematic Universe release, however, it means much of the movie remains a mystery. (We're still no clearer on whether Robert Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom is actually a Tony Stark variant or not, despite Marvel Studios head Kevin Feige's recent comments.) That stated, the latest tease did contain several notable moments that have only served to increase the already significant hype.

Recent findings suggest that the fresh "Doomsday" trailer finally gives Cyclops the X-Men line fans were waiting for, when Marsden's hero delivers his "To me, my X-Men" rallying cry to assemble his mutants, the Avengers, Fantastic Four, and several other heroes. But beyond that tantalizing glimpse at the film's massive showdown, there are several other notable moments, and lucky for you, we've gone and rounded 'em up.

The precise plot of "Avengers: Doomsday" remains under wraps for now, but at this point, we can pretty much piece together the major beats. Previously, co-director Joe Russo told Empire that Robert Downey Jr.'s Victor Von Doom is a "father who's a victim of trauma" and that he "lost a child." That lined up with what we've seen in previous trailers, wherein Vanessa Kirby's Sue Storm/Invisible Woman talked about how Doom "used to be different" before "everything he loved was taken from him." Now, the latest "Doomsday" trailer has confirmed that the Avengers themselves are responsible for it all.

In the fresh trailer, Chris Evans' Steve Rogers can be heard saying, "Years ago, we did what was needed to make the world right," in reference to the events of 2019's "Avengers: Endgame." He continues: "But we didn't know those choices would have consequences." It seems that Steve's choice to travel back through time to be with his lover, Peggy Carter (Hayley Atwell) — and whatever the Avengers did to defeat Josh Brolin's Thanos — caused some sort of multiversal upheaval in which Doom's daughter met her, well, doom.

In a recent development, this is why RDJ's villain tells the heroes of "Doomsday" that they've been living "stolen lives." With Steve's speech in the latest trailer, it's all but certain he and the Avengers are responsible for whatever killed Doom's daughter, and likely the multiversal collapse referenced in the "Avengers Endgame: Encore" TVA scene. Turns out, Doom is the "consequence" to which Steve refers.

Thanks to what seemed like a hasty casting announcement prior to the final "Avengers: Doomsday" trailer, we knew Hailee Steinfeld's Kate Bishop would be appearing in the movie. Now, the trailer has given us our first look at the heir to the Hawkeye mantle in a very quick shot that shows her looking up at something that's clearly got her very worried. But Kate might be just one of the Young Avengers to appear in the film.

We know Scott Lang's (Paul Rudd) daughter, Cassie Lang (Kathryn Newton), is also part of "Doomsday." She reveals up briefly in the latest trailer, too, looking as concerned as Kate. Interestingly enough, both characters are in their superhero suits, which suggests they'll be joining the massive fight against Doctor Doom. That means two members of the Young Avengers will be involved in "Doomsday." Marvel Studios has yet to officially introduce these heroes as the superhero group from the comics, but has been slowly building up this new generation of Avengers over the past few years.

The only likely member of the Young Avengers who hasn't appeared in trailers and is yet to be confirmed as being involved with "Doomsday" is Iman Vellani's Ms. Marvel. According to Andy Serkis, Ms. Marvel will appear in "Doomsday," but Marvel hasn't made that official. Otherwise, there are a handful of other young heroes that could show up and potentially form the Young Avengers proper in the movie itself, including Riri Williams/Ironheart (Dominique Thorne) and America Chavez (Xochitl Gomez). For now, it looks more likely than ever we'll see an official Young Avengers group unite in "Doomsday.".

Recent findings suggest that the new "Avengers: Doomsday" trailer highlights Chris Hemsworth's Thor rising from the floor surrounded by yellow lightning as opposed to his typical blue lightning. That's significant, as it all but confirms he'll be wielding a powerful new force known as the Odinforce. This power, created by the Kings of Asgard, is a major upgrade for the character, and the latest trailer appears to have shown it in action.

One of the most frequently showcased "Doomsday" scenes thus far has been the moment in which Thor debuts himself at Doctor Doom, only to be stopped mid-air and flung backwards by the villain's formidable force (which, as it happens, involves a Jacky Kirby-inspired energy blast from Doom). Clearly, the God of Thunder is as outmatched as the rest of his cohorts.

But back when the first four teaser trailers for "Doomsday" dropped, we saw Hemsworth's hero begging his father for the "strength of the All-Fathers." Since then we've seen concept art and a "Doomsday" billboard that seemingly spoiled the fact Thor was getting a major upgrade in the form of the Odinforce. It's this force that turns his lightning yellow, and the final "Doomsday" trailer is the first time we see footage of it in action. The brief shot demonstrates Thor ascending in a forest, which looks to be the same forest in which he begged for the strength of the All-Fathers in the original teaser. Looks like he got his wish. Whether it will prove effective against Doom, however, remains to be seen.

Recent findings suggest that we got our first look at the X-Men in "Avengers: Doomsday" courtesy of the X-Men-heavy trailer back in January 2026. Since then, we've learned how the mutants might find their way to the Avengers. The film will take place during the collapse of the multiverse, whereby several "incursions" will see planets and timelines collide. These collisions are likely to be the reason for the film's major crossovers, i.e. the Fox-era X-Men and the Fantastic Four arriving on the Avengers' Earth 616. But it seems when the X-Men and Avengers first come face to face they initially clash, as evidenced by footage from prior trailers in which Yelena Belova/Black Widow (Florence Pugh) takes on Mystique (Rebecca Romijn) and Shang-Chi (Simu Liu) battles Gambit (Channing Tatum).

It has been revealed that now, however, the final "Doomsday" trailer has confirmed that Anthony Mackie's Sam Wilson/Captain America will face off against James Marsden's Scott Summers/Cyclops. The trailer shows the pair going toe-to-toe in what looks to be a pretty brutal clash, with Wilson holding Cyclops by the neck as he unleashes an optic blast. Clearly, the X-Men and Avengers ultimately manage to, as Thor puts it, "put aside their petty squabbles." But for at least a moment, the two superhero teams will be at odds in the movie, and Sam Wilson's showdown with Scott Summers looks set to be a major highlight.

Industry observers note that the final "Avengers: Doomsday" trailer reminds us of the main threat facing Earth 616 in the movie. While Doctor Doom is the substantial bad, the entire multiverse is collapsing, and in the latest trailer we see a brief shot that highlights two planets in the sky above New York City. The trailer also features several shots of heroes looking up at the sky, or out of windows and reacting with shock and dismay, and it's likely this planetary incursion is what has them so upset.

According to recent reports, we've known that the heroes of "Doomsday" would be dealing with multiversal collapse in the film for some time. But this is the first shot we've seen in an official trailer that highlights planets on a collision course with Earth. Previously, a Dunkin' Donuts commercial gave us our best look at the threat the Avengers face in "Doomsday," with a shot showing a planet looming in the sky over Avengers Tower. But it looks as though multiple timelines/planets are set to collide with Earth based on the brief scene from this latest trailer.

Industry observers note that exactly which planets these are remains unclear. One may in fact be the Fox-era X-Men's world, and this cityscape view could be giving us a glimpse of their arrival in the Avengers' timeline. Either way, clearly the stakes have never been higher, as failure means the complete and utter destruction of the multiverse.

"Avengers: Doomsday" hits theaters on December 18, 2026.

The Voice newbie Riley Green is having a killer first season on NBC’s long-running singing competition, which is at the moment airing on the 2026 TV schedule. He easily won over the majority of the country music hopefuls during the Blind Auditions and has given the competitors excellent advice that they can continue to carry with them. But no competition is smooth sailing, and the “Don’t Mind If I Do” singer is revealing the toughest part of coaching.

With the Live Shows in full swing, the country hit maker has two of Season 30’s strongest contenders, Joe Henley and Ferryn & Brinkley, still on his team. As we move ever closer to the unveiling of the winning coach and star, Green, who can right now claim the title of being one of 2026’s Sexiest Men Alive, has struggled with having to send so many talented singers home. He told People why he’s having fun during the live performances:.

Recent findings suggest that I’m really excited that I’m not having to send people home. That was the toughest thing about what’s gone on so far. It was tough in the auditions because you hear these amazing stories that people have... and they’re taking off to come try to chase their dreams, and maybe they don’t get picked.

Nobody is ever really an overnight sensation, so The Voice’s superstar coaches absolutely understand what it’s like to chase your dreams and have setbacks along the way. I can’t imagine how agonizing it must be to know you have to send home some really talented singers. Whether you’re rookie Queen Latifah or veteran coach Adam Levine, cutting someone’s dream short never gets any easier. So, I get why Green is relieved to just sit back and enjoy the performances, and leave it up to the audience to decide who continues on and who gets cut.

In an interesting twist for Season 30, the Live Shows have replaced the Knockouts, which happen to be Levine’s least favorite part of the competition for a very similar reason. No The Voice coach wants to have to send home talented singers, and leaving it all in America’s hands takes the pressure off the coaches. The Marshals guest star also stated this about his experienceon the show:.

Worse than that is once you’ve worked with them and they are on your team and then having to send them home after that, I’m so sick of having to make those decisions. So I’m glad America can do it, and I’ll just try to help them along the way.

One of the best parts of the reality competition show is watching how the coaches really become fans of their own team members. Kelly Clarkson has expressed her commitment to continue collaborating with Team Kelly, and I’m sure other coaches feel just as dedicated to creating such a supportive atmosphere.

Sources indicate that I wouldn’t be surprised to see Green touring or doing special performances with his Team Riley singers, especially considering how connected he sounds like he feels with all of them. Also, it would probably go a long way toward making him feel better for those departing contestants.

The Voice Season 30 continues to air on Mondays until December 14th, when a two-hour finale will reveal who is crowned the winner. You can also watch the next day with a Peacock subscription. And Season 31’s The Voice: Celebrity is already waiting in the wings with fresh host Keke Palmer.

25 Years Later, GTA 3 Is Still the Most Fascinating Open-World Experiment

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that it’s October 2001, and you’re standing in a dimly lit game store, where rows upon rows of boxes sit in anticipation as you glance across their titles, unsure exactly which among them you'll end up taking home.
  • In a recent development, the artwork’s nothing to write home about, just a collage of pictures in red, blue, and green hues, featuring obscure faces, a police chopper, and a car up in flames.
  • It has been revealed that grand Theft Auto 3 was a jolt of raw adrenaline.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that it’s October 2001, and you’re standing in a dimly lit game store, where rows upon rows of boxes sit in anticipation as you glance across their titles, unsure exactly which among them you'll end up taking home. Unfortunately, you can only pick one. Your eyes are already darting between Devil May Cry, Silent Hill 2, and Ico, which all feel eerily attuned to those pre-Halloween vibes. Noticing your indecisiveness (and the look of impatience on your mother’s face), the store clerk strides over with an assist, placing in your hands a game you had never heard of until that very moment.

In a recent development, the artwork’s nothing to write home about, just a collage of pictures in red, blue, and green hues, featuring obscure faces, a police chopper, and a car up in flames. Your instinct is to just go with your gut; Silent Hill 2 is what you came here for, after all. But something’s telling you otherwise. Maybe it’s the store clerk going on about its open-world premise, or the name itself that strikes a chord within you. Whatever reason incites it, you make the ultimate decision. Little did you know, you’d be walking home with one of the greatest achievements in video game history.

It has been revealed that grand Theft Auto 3 was a jolt of raw adrenaline. It was a paradigm shift that made the possibilities of 3D open-world design feel almost limitless. The game thrust players into what Rockstar co-founder Dan Houser described as “an old, post-industrial American city,” a mash-up of Chicago, Pittsburgh, Detroit, Philly, and mostly New York teeming with grim alleyways, pedestrian-filled streets, and sky-slicing buildings that eclipsed many of the incredible worlds that came before it, from The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time to Driver. It was called Liberty City. No game had molded such immense verticality into a 3D world that felt like a living ecosystem where the inhabitants and environments reacted to you directly. It was a feat many at the time considered impossible on existing hardware — and Rockstar did it with virtually no load times to boot.

According to recent reports, like nearly every title the studio would develop for the system, GTA 3 pushed the PlayStation 2 to its absolute limits. Developers DMA Design (now known as Rockstar North) had to cleverly stream around 130MB of data, including 3D animations, textures, models, and audio, through the PS2’s 32MB of system RAM. For perspective, just one Liberty City island amounted to roughly 50MB of static geometry. To make it all work, the team engineered a dynamic streaming system that fetched sectors of the map ahead of the player, while purging the city behind them. It’s why you’d often see the city pop in and populate right in front of you if you were driving at top speeds and quickly looked behind the character. When code couldn't bridge the gap, Rockstar cleverly designed curved roads to slow down sports cars, added subtle aerodynamic drag to prevent vehicles from outrunning the laser reader, and capped active traffic to eight models. What technical leads Adam Fowler, Obbe Vermeij, and their colleagues accomplished with GTA 3 was nothing short of magic.

In a recent development, technical limitations weren’t the only roadblocks for Rockstar. Following the release of GTA 2, which he felt suffered from a lack of narrative thrust due to its non-linear design, Houser set out to give GTA 3 a far more complex story. With the help of co-writer James Worrall, they devised localized character "hubs" that served as contacts for missions, like Joey Leone, Toni Cipriani, and Salvatore Leone. Rather than treating open-world freedom and story progression as opposing forces, Houser used these dynamic webs to bridge the gap, tying mission arcs directly to specific territories and turf wars. That allowed GTA 3’s story to organically teach players the city's layouts and mechanics, moving through the industrial side of Portland with Toni Cipriani, navigating the Leone family's criminal empire with Salvatore, and eventually venturing into Staunton Island's political corruption and corporate underbelly. Each latest contact pulled Claude deeper into Liberty City's criminal ecosystem, gradually opening up new territories while revealing another layer of the city's interconnected underworld. Coupled with the decision to keep Claude a silent protagonist, the hub structure allowed players to chart their own path without sacrificing the momentum of a cohesive crime saga.

The radio stations of GTA 3 also gave it that extra level of immersion, but before Rockstar could throw cash at some of the biggest names in the industry, the developers had to improvise with completely original music. Led by audio directors Craig Conner and Stuart Ross, the team wrote and recorded genre-specific tracks under aliases, like “Lucy,” “The Mudds,” “Marydances,” “Da Shootaz,” and more. Ross and Conner were also responsible for the GTA 3 Main Theme, a moody, “dark jazz” track inspired by The Sopranos and Goodfellas, which is still one of the best in the series. Combining underground hip-hop, drum & bass, and licensed classics from Giorgio Moroder’s Scarface score, the team was able to capture a gritty realism in the sounds of Liberty City. It’s a testament to Rockstar’s sonic ingenuity, one that finds a kind of spiritual successor in GTA 6, which features original scoring by French electronic duo Justice. The tools have changed, but the underlying idea remains the same: original music can give a fictional city an identity all its own.

It has been revealed that what elevated these stations even further was GTA’s name-brand comedy, still in its infancy but just as hilarious, brought to life in Chatterbox FM. Scripted by Houser and hosted by Lazlow Jones, the talk-radio station's absurd caller rants and SNL-like commercial parodies gave Liberty City a lived-in texture long before you ever stepped out of your (likely stolen) vehicle. An especially on-the-nose example is a first-time-caller mother who rants about parenting in the age of video games: “I let my kid play video games, and now he runs around the house looking for gold coins. This is teaching our children to go chase money!” One of my personal favorites involves a suitably redneck-sounding character raving about how “guns don’t kill people, death kills people.” They go on to add: “You can’t die from a bullet, you can die from a cardiac arrest or organ failure or major hemorrhage. Small piece of metal ain’t the problem.” It’s no wonder Chatterbox is still widely considered some of the funniest and most satirical writing in the entire GTA series, though GTA 6 is shaping up to give GTA 3 a run for its comedy gold.

It has been revealed that A weekly cheat sheet to what you’ll eventually love to play. No buying, no commitment — just saving for later.

On the heels of 9/11, released just 41 days after those fatal terrorist attacks, GTA 3 also remains a strange time capsule. Rockstar delayed the game by a few weeks to surgically scrub dialogue and a mission referencing terrorism, and changed the city’s squad cars from blue-and-white NYPD knockoffs to generic black-and-whites. Even the original box art was scrapped in North America, giving birth to the now-iconic grid layout that emblazons the cover of every series follow-up. Yet beyond those surface-level tweaks, the game took on a surreal weight in the wake of the tragedy. Having grown up just across the river in Upcoming Jersey, the attacks were an inextricable part of my life, even if much of the chaos of that era remains a blur. But I’ll never forget the long nights spent driving through Liberty City in the shadow of such devastation. Steering through those dark and rainy streets felt hauntingly poignant; a digital New York pulsing with life at a moment when the real world had suddenly ground to a painful halt.

GTA 3 was a baseball bat to the face of the gaming industry at a time when it was flourishing. It landed in the same year as Ico, Silent Hill 2, Halo: Combat Evolved, Final Fantasy 10, and Metal Gear Solid 2. Even in the face of such greatness, Grand Theft Auto 3 is unparalleled in its scope, bridging some of the most sophisticated world design ever attempted with a bespoke narrative engine that forever changed gaming. No one stated it better than Sam Houser, who told IGN in 2001: “It has its own personality in a way I've never seen before in a game, to the point where it actually becomes part of the gameplay experience.”.

It has been revealed that personality. That's what has always made Grand Theft Auto one of the most compelling entertainment properties on the planet, and GTA 3 was where that personality truly came into its own. 25 years later, with Rockstar's dominant open-world adventure being the latest example, Liberty City remains a testament to how ambition and clever design can fundamentally reshape an entire medium.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that in 2021, at the recommendation of a film producer, the writer and showrunner Rebecca Cutter read a pulpy murder-mystery novel on a flight from her native Massachusetts to her current base in Los Angeles. By the time she landed, Cutter had finished the book and was already mapping out the TV adaptation in her head.

The plot heavily involved a Texas abortion clinic, and the state had just passed SB 8, one of the country’s most restrictive abortion bills until Roe v. Wade was overturned the following year. As she contemplated bringing The Hunting Wives to life, Cutter saw the political stakes come into focus as well.

“I started thinking about the ‘red state, blue state’ of it,” she tells Vanity Fair ahead of the show’s season two premiere on Thursday. “What if…we really play this culture war?”.

“I don’t think I do gratuitous sex scenes,” says showrunner Rebecca Cutter. “I think you always are seeing a power dynamic play out or a plot point play out.”.

The result was one of Netflix’s biggest breakout hits in recent years, sent up in a Saturday Night Live sketch as the “straight but lesbian, horny Republican murder drama.” As a show, Hunting Wives amps up the noirish aspects of the suspense thriller written by May Cobb, a native of the East Texas Piney Woods, and adds a heaping dose of MAGA-adjacent camp. Cutter finishes the mix with plenty of sex scenes, particularly between Malin Akerman’s Margo, a femme fatale partly inspired by Melania Trump who is married to a Republican gubernatorial hopeful, and Brittany Snow’s Sophie, a liberal do-gooder who, like Cutter, arrives in town from a blue corner of Massachusetts. (Cutter was raised in Cambridge and graduated from Wesleyan University, the Connecticut liberal arts college known for its progressive politics and pipeline to Hollywood.).

Recent findings suggest that hunting Wives executive producer Erwin Stoff told Cutter he’d pay for her to go to Texas to meet Cobb and breathe the Piney Woods air herself. She met Cobb’s father and her best friend from high school. She shot skeet with the women—she even got it in three, just as Sophie does in the first season. At a high-end Dallas shopping area where the likes of Gucci can be found, Cutter got a better sense of the hair, clothes, and bodies of her eventual characters. “I understand the notion that Sophie could be amused and entertained and intrigued by these women,” Cutter notes, “and eventually seduced.”.

Recent findings suggest that cutter thinks of the show primarily in terms of its tonal mash-up: “I think we managed to wrangle it into one piece of art,” she indicates, “but there’s comedy, there’s violence, there’s noir, there’s soap, there’s earnest emotion.” To the extent that she assigned any political beliefs to the rich white women of Cobb’s novel, it was in the spirit of grounding her characters in the specifics of their world. Still, as we speak, Cutter decides “to get real with it.”.

Cutter on set. She describes Sophie, a fellow native of blue Massachusetts, as a surrogate for her own awakening to MAGA Texas.

Sources indicate that “The whole thing was a little bit of a parable, in my mind, of how you could fall for someone like [Donald] Trump,” she admits. “Sophie has her principles, but they only go so far. They end right where something starts to make her feel good.” Cutter was as curious as anyone else from her educated milieu about the quirkier aspects of Trump, like the Diet Coke button he had installed on the Resolute Desk. How liberating must it feel to embrace a movement so openly untethered from the pieties of politics and taste?

“Not that my show is a deep dive on Trump,” Cutter says, “but maybe there is an element that’s sort of looking under the hood.”.

Recent findings suggest that the twisted love story between Margo and Sophie entangles all of the wealthy, hard-drinking, gun-toting women in their orbit, and its central killing—one of several propelling the show forward, with a third season slated to begin filming this year—stems from an effort to cover up Margo’s abortion as her NRA-loving husband plots his political ascent. (In this proudly oversexed town, he has his own share of affairs.) Hunting Wives is the rare Netflix soap to receive steady coverage from mainstream national outlets; the fascination undoubtedly has something to do with the impression that, like Yellowstone or Morgan Wallen before it, the show unlocks something about MAGA’s cultural staying power. In a Fresh York Times guest essay this month that evaluated the post-2024 Hollywood landscape, Sharon Waxman, the editor in chief of The Wrap, wrote, “From Melania on Amazon’s streaming service to The Hunting Wives on Netflix to the ever-expanding Taylor Sheridan universe on Paramount+ to Bari Weiss’s being put in charge of CBS News, the vibe shift was visible on all our screens.”.

Margo and her politically ambitious husband are partners in subterfuge and debauchery.

It has been revealed that cutter indicates she had no particular agenda nor any “ultra-evil villain strategy of how it was going to be received or how it would be culturally relevant.” But Hunting Wives is sprinkled with enough proper nouns—a Peter Thiel mention here, a Walmart reference there—and distinctly modern aesthetics that she can acknowledge its appeal as something of a Rosetta stone for the moment in MAGA femininity. Even in the ostensibly waning days of the movement, the plastic surgery and soaring heels continue to captivate and horrify coastal elites. Cutter says that Callie (Jaime Ray Newman), another of Margo’s lovers, has a bit of Kristi Noem and Marjorie Taylor Greene in her: that “sort of slightly butch, real gun, real ‘back the blue’ [element]…the toughness of those women.”.

It has been revealed that the second season of Hunting Wives maintains the slipperiness that keeps the show from veering into moralism; it stands apart from other Trump-era art in its refusal to take sides. “I think I remember, in the pitch, someone saying, ‘But will red-state people like it too?’” Cutter recalls. “I was like, ‘I think so.’” Both Margo and Sophie are awash in their respective red and blue stereotypes, but neither is more admirable than the other. Their sordid union is a testament to the flexibility of both their principles and their preferences. From one vantage, it is, in the end, all about sex.

Recent findings suggest that “Margo is the symbol of freedom and sexuality and feminine power and empoweredness and selfishness that [Sophie] feels she’s lost,” Cutter says, adding that Akerman’s comfort in such a role helped drive her liberal use of physical intimacy. “The audience may disagree with me,” she says, but “I don’t think I do gratuitous sex scenes. I think you always are seeing a power dynamic play out or a plot point play out.” Last year, though, when Netflix acquired Hunting Wives, which was initially ordered by Starz in 2023, Cutter had a more practical concern.

“I literally googled,” she recalls, “‘Does Netflix show boobs?’”.

Six Things You Should Do Now to Optimize Your Setup for GTA 6

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1147 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, you’re almost ready for Grand Theft Auto VI.
  • Sources indicate that GTA 6 is absurdly large.
  • Alternatively, it’s pretty easy to add more storage (if you can afford it).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, you’re almost ready for Grand Theft Auto VI. You’ve preloaded the game on your console, you’ve taken the next month off work, and you’ve locked your phone in a Faraday cage and set it adrift at sea. You’re prepared to lock in, and you haven’t forgotten a thing…right? Well, just to make sure, here are the most important tips to optimize your setup before you fire up the most anticipated game of the decade.

Sources indicate that GTA 6 is absurdly large. According to Rockstar, you’ll need up to 212GB of storage space. For high-end consoles like the PS5 Pro, that’s more than 10% of the available storage space, and close to half the space on the more budget-conscious Xbox Series S. There’s a good chance you’ll have to delete something to make room.

Alternatively, it’s pretty easy to add more storage (if you can afford it). External SSDs are probably the cheapest route, though you’ll want to make sure to use a high-speed USB cable to connect it. It’s even worth shopping around for alternate models of SSD. For example, at the time of writing, the popular 2TB WD_BLACK external drive was close to $200, but the exact same drive in pink was $132.

In a recent development, you can also directly upgrade the storage of your console with expansion drives. The Xbox Series X|S supports proprietary expansion cards, while the PS5 and PS5 Pro can accept most M.2 internal SSDs. These will generally be faster, since they plug directly into the console via higher-speed connections than a drive hooked up via USB.

It has been revealed that let’s face it: Half the fun of any sandbox game is the weird, unique stuff that happens to only you. So you’re probably going to be hitting that “record recent gameplay” button more often than usual. While you’re cleaning up your storage space (or adding more), make sure to account for all the video clips you might want to save.

It has been revealed that file size of video clips depends on a lot of factors, but 4K recordings can generally take up to 0.5GB per minute of footage. You can cut that down by saving footage in 1080p instead, but either way you’ll want to leave a little extra space.

In a recent development, game footage is also a pretty good place to look if you need to make room on your console and don’t want to delete any games. Be honest with yourself: You don’t need all those clips from Horizon Forbidden West you saved four years ago. Dive into the settings on your console and find the biggest media files you forgot you even had on there.

Sources indicate that according to Rockstar, GTA 6 will be targeting 30fps across consoles at launch, which is pretty low as modern AAA games go. Part of the reason for that is all the processing power going to rendering a complex environment, but it also means you won’t need a fancy high frame rate TV or monitor any time soon to get the most out of it. Still, it couldn’t hurt to check a few settings on your display.

Recent findings suggest that first, make sure you’re using a higher refresh rate than 30Hz. While the game is targeting 30fps, it is technically capable of more, so if your console can keep up, you don’t want to accidentally bottleneck your frames. This setting will vary by device, so check the manual that came with your screen.

Also, make sure you have HDR enabled on your hardware. There’s a good chance this is already turned on for your TV, but sometimes other devices can switch display modes if they only support SDR. The game will help you calibrate your HDR settings for GTA 6 specifically when you launch it, but only if it detects HDR compatibility in the first place.

If you’re planning to buy a console specifically for GTA 6, this might be one of those rare instances where a PS5 Pro really is worth the upgrade. According to Rockstar, certain features like ray-traced shadows will only be available on the Pro version of Sony’s console.

More importantly, the PS5 Pro version supports PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (or PSSR), which upscales lower-resolution images to get better detail and higher frame rates out of the same hardware. Given that GTA 6 is already starting at a meager target of 30fps on most consoles, anything that can give your frame rate a boost is probably going to feel like a welcome improvement over the baseline.

I’ll tell you a secret as someone who’s spent a lot of time testing different game controllers: Most of the time, you really don’t need an expensive “elite” controller. Most of the time. I don’t buy into the idea that a taller control stick is going to make you an esports athlete. It can be nice to have, but it’s not a game changer. What does matter is customizing your controls, especially for long gaming sessions.

The DualSense Edge wireless controller is a favorite of mine, mainly because of the rear paddles and adjustable triggers. The former lets you map any button to a rear lever that you can access with your fingers underneath the controller, which can often ease some of the wrist strain of awkward button combos. And the adjustable triggers let you activate the buttons with less motion, again reducing repetitive stress.

According to recent reports, the Xbox Elite Series 2 controller has similar features for the Xbox, as well as custom caps for the D-pad. Both consoles’ versions of pro controllers are more expensive than the standard ones, but if you’re planning to game for many hours, it can be worth it to get a controller that’s more comfortable for you.

If you have an Xbox One, you don’t necessarily have to upgrade your console to play GTA 6, but you might want to take a look at your network. GTA 6 will be available on Xbox Cloud Gaming on day one, and you’ll be able to stream the game to an Xbox One console (as long as you purchase Cloud playtime as well or get some with your Game Pass subscription). This is the only way to play on a console older than the current generation, so if you don’t want to shell out for new hardware, this might be your best bet.

Xbox recommends a minimum of a 20Mbps connection to run cloud gaming, but more is obviously better. If you can connect your console to a wired Ethernet connection, that would be better and provide more stability. If you can’t connect a cable, then at least make sure you’re well within range of your wifi router, and try to limit any other bandwidth-hogging applications on the network while you’re playing.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • No TV writer is as synonymous with their creation as Rod Serling is with "The Twilight Zone." As the show's host, he was the face of the series.
  • Recent findings suggest that serling wrote 92 of the 156 "Twilight Zone" episodes that aired during the show's five season run.
  • "Perchance to Dream" stars Richard Conte (nowadays most remembered for playing Don Barzini in "The Godfather") as Edward Hall, a man who hasn't slept for days — because he's convinced if he falls asleep, he'll die.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

No TV writer is as synonymous with their creation as Rod Serling is with "The Twilight Zone." As the show's host, he was the face of the series. In an anthology series, you can't expect to see the same actors and characters every time you tune in, so the only familiar sound to welcome you into the twilight zone was Serling's calm, sardonic voice.

Recent findings suggest that serling wrote 92 of the 156 "Twilight Zone" episodes that aired during the show's five season run. The first episode that did not come from a Serling script is the series' ninth episode, "Perchance to Dream," with writer Charles Beaumont self-adapting a short story he originally wrote for publication in Playboy magazine. (Now, technically, the beloved eighth "Twilight Zone" episode "Time Enough At Last," boasting one of the show's most depressing endings, was based on a short story by Lynn Venable. However, Serling wrote the teleplay.).

"Perchance to Dream" stars Richard Conte (nowadays most remembered for playing Don Barzini in "The Godfather") as Edward Hall, a man who hasn't slept for days — because he's convinced if he falls asleep, he'll die. But his insomnia is born of a different medical condition. Hall has a weak heart, so much so that if he experiences a significant enough shock, even in his dreams, it might literally kill him. The episode sees Hall visiting a psychiatrist, Dr. Eliot Rathmann (John Larch), and recalling how his own mind seems to be trying to knock him off a ledge with terrifying dreams.

The title "Perchance to Dream" comes from a soliloquy in "Hamlet," when the eponymous prince muses: "To sleep, perchance to dream." But Hamlet is talking about the sleep of death and his temptation to suicide. That makes the line a fitting, though flipped-on-its-head, title for a story about a man terrified he'll die if he falls asleep. ("Batman: The Animated Series" would later use "Perchance to Dream" as the title for star Kevin Conroy's favorite episode.).

Recent findings suggest that the episode is primarily set in Dr. Rathmann's skyscraper office, but peeks inside Hall's dreams to let us see his terror. The second half cuts between the office and Hall recounting his dreams of a carnival, where "everything [is] warped and twisted out of shape," and the nightmare that came closest to killing him. A cat-eyed woman named Maya (Suzanne Lloyd) leads Hall down a haunted trail, packed with monstrous animatronics, and then onto a roller coaster.

Maya's feline coding marks her as a predator, toying with Hall like a terrified mouse trying to escape her claws. Watching the episode now, it feels like "A Nightmare on Elm Street" with a femme fatale instead of a knife-handed slasher. The carnival scenes use Dutch angles and foggy camera filters feel extra unnerving and wrong. Combined with the Halloween aesthetic and Maya's cutting laughter, the dream lives up to the nightmare that Hall described.

Charles Beaumont remained one of most prolific "Twilight Zone" writers. During the second season, he self-adapted his spooky short story "The Howling Man," helping turn it into one of the scariest "Twilight Zone" episodes ever. But "Perchance to Dream" first proved that Beaumont could makes trips to the Twilight Zone genuinely terror-inducing.

In a recent development, the X4 Classic and the X3 improve on the original X4 with quality-of-life upgrades like a larger battery, relocated page-turn buttons, a real-time clock, and a tilt-to-turn-page feature. They're also lighter and thinner than the X4, though there is a trade-off involved: They drop the USB-C charging port in favor of magnetic pogo pins that require a separate adapter (included).

Either is a great option for those who prioritize crisp, readable text above the conveniences of a built-in light or touchscreen, as those add extra layers between the inner screen and outer glass. It's also crucial to understand what you're getting into: These devices support only e-books without Digital Rights Management (DRM), which means you can't use it to read your existing library of Kindle books. On the plus side, there's no longer a need to worry about flashing newly introduced firmware if you don't want to, as the native version has been totally overhauled and is now one of your best options (though the new firmware, called "Licorice," isn't available on the X3 quite yet).
